_note: The proverbs of Northcote W. Thomas, Anthropological Report on the
Ibo-Speaking Peoples of Nigeria, Part VI: Proverbs, Stories, Tones in
Ibo (1914), restored from a damaged scan.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
The scan reads the Igbo badly: Thomas transcribed Asaba-district speech
phonetically in 1913, and the scanner turns ị and ọ into y, p, q, ç or §
depending on the letterform. So the text was read back by a model that was
given BOTH the damaged Igbo and the English Thomas printed beneath it, and
told to undo the scanner rather than to translate. Every English here is
Thomas’s own sense, repaired; nothing was invented.
WHAT EACH ENTRY CARRIES
igbo        the proverb in standard Igbo orthography
english     Thomas’s meaning, with scan damage repaired
usage       his note on when the proverb is used, where he gave one
dialect     the town it was collected in, where the marker could be placed
theme       one of the eleven themes /proverbs filters by
confidence  high | medium | low — how settled the restoration is
Low-confidence readings are published rather than dropped, and the proverb
page says so where they appear. A reader who does not speak Igbo loses the
proverb entirely if they are hidden, and the alternative — quietly keeping
only the easy ones — would misrepresent how much of the book is legible.

proverbs.igbo: Ọnwụ gbụ utu, gbụ eze; ihe agwụ, aka agwụsie.
proverbs.english: Death kills the penis, kills the teeth; when a thing is exhausted, the hand is exhausted.
proverbs.usage: When a man toils and saves, and grows old.

proverbs.igbo: Asị ngwere, isi akịka eju gị; amaghị nke ga-acha.
proverbs.english: They say the lizard's head is full of spots, but it does not know which will turn red-headed.
proverbs.usage: A man has many children, no one knows who will get rich.

proverbs.igbo: A dighi ezute onye riri ụnya.
proverbs.english: They never meet one who ate yesterday.
proverbs.usage: To a thief who tries to rival a rich man by stealing.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ sị nwata, ị na-akwa akwa na nne gị jere ahịa madụ; ọ bụzi nke m ọ ga-esi mee?
proverbs.english: He says to the child: 'You are crying that your mother went to the people's market; if she went to mine, how would it be?'
proverbs.usage: Of a man who laments lack of money.

proverbs.igbo: Ụwa adịghị mma madụ, ike eji nji.
proverbs.english: If the world is hard for a man, his buttocks are black.
proverbs.usage: A rich man does not talk of a poor man's troubles till the poor man talks of them.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ ka onye na-emeri onye iwe.
proverbs.english: One who surpasses one, conquers him.
proverbs.usage: A small man with money can purchase help.

proverbs.igbo: Ọnụ ite adịghị esi ite akpọ.
proverbs.english: The neck of a pot does not break with the pot.
proverbs.usage: A rich man leaves his property when he dies.

proverbs.igbo: Ara dị okpọrọ n'obi adịghị ekwe ka nwoke wahapụ ya.
proverbs.english: A woman's breast does not let men keep far from her.
proverbs.usage: When a poor man depends on (sponges on) a rich man and won't be driven away.

proverbs.igbo: Amadi adịghị ana ogbenye nwa.
proverbs.english: A rich man does not take a poor man's child.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ dị afị adịghị ana ogbenye nwa.
proverbs.english: A rich man never takes away a poor man's child.
proverbs.usage: A poor man can say this in misfortune.

proverbs.igbo: Ọsa hụrụ aha, agụọ aha nwa.
proverbs.english: If the squirrel sees a name, it names a child.
proverbs.usage: When a man admires a rich man's house (and has no money to build in the same way).

proverbs.igbo: Ọ nọ ala, akpata igwe aka.
proverbs.english: He sits down and touches the sky.
proverbs.usage: A rich man sends and his work is done.

proverbs.igbo: Ụwa agwụghị.
proverbs.english: The world does not finish; your children may suffer for you.
proverbs.usage: If a rich man harasses a poor man for nothing.

proverbs.igbo: Iyi atara, obodi egbu azụ n'elu ugwu.
proverbs.english: The stream dries up, a fool kills fish on the hill.
proverbs.usage: Good things always go to the rich.

proverbs.igbo: Ogbenye nwere enyi, ọdara anara ya.
proverbs.english: The poor man gets a friend; the rich man takes him away.

proverbs.igbo: Ntakịrị adịghị agwụ n'gbọọlọ onye na-ata ọchị.
proverbs.english: A little palm wine stops in the calabash of the palm wine maker.
proverbs.usage: A rich man is never reduced to poverty.

proverbs.igbo: Mmadụ ma nwe ndụ, mmiri ọnụ anaghị eti ya n'ihu eze.
proverbs.english: If a man has life, the rain (? saliva) will not beat the front of his teeth.
proverbs.usage: A child of a rich man will not go under in a palaver.

proverbs.igbo: Ngwụrọ abụọ na-eje n'ụzọ ije, gburu nnụ anọ ijiji.
proverbs.english: Two lame men walking in the road killed four hundred flies.
proverbs.usage: If two rich men travel, each makes his own arrangements.

proverbs.igbo: Anyị je n'ebe ọgaranya, ka anyị bụrụ; onye je n'ebe ogbenye akalị mma.
proverbs.english: We go to the house of a rich man that we may become so; he who goes to a poor man is better off.
proverbs.usage: The poor are more generous than the rich.

proverbs.igbo: Ọjịrị anaghị atụfu ego, ọ na-ada ogbenye mgbe ọ nwụrụ.
proverbs.english: A rich man does not throw away money; he is poor when he dies.

proverbs.igbo: Ọnọdụ otu ebe na-ato ọla.
proverbs.english: Sitting in one place makes one sleepy; riches make a man forget his fellows.

proverbs.igbo: Anya adịghị onye ara ka ọ rie ngwere; ọ nweghị ụlọ ọ ga-eri ya.
proverbs.english: A madman desires to eat a lizard; there is no house to eat it in.
proverbs.usage: Not all can become rich.

proverbs.igbo: Eze kpere ikpe, ọ na-elo ọnụma; eze kwuputara ọnụma, ani agwụ n'aka ya.
proverbs.english: The king complains, he stops vexation; if the king speaks out his wrath, the town finishes in his hand.
proverbs.usage: When the rich oppresses the poor.

proverbs.igbo: Onye ji elu, ya kwaa ya rie; ya hapụ mma nwa ogbenye ji n'aka ya.
proverbs.english: Whose yams are done, let him eat; let him leave the knife of the child of the poor man which he has in his hand to him.
proverbs.usage: When the rich and the poor quarrel, the poor man says this.

proverbs.igbo: Nwa ọhụ amaghị onye kpụrụ isi ya.
proverbs.english: A baby does not know who shaves its head; a rich man does not know the one who gave him a start.

proverbs.igbo: Onye enweghị, mmadụ ibe enyeghị ya.
proverbs.english: Who has none, others do not give to him.
proverbs.usage: Said by a poor man with rich brothers.

proverbs.igbo: Nke afụ onye adịghị afụ ibe.
proverbs.english: What troubles one does not trouble another.
proverbs.usage: A poor man has health, a rich man is sick.

proverbs.igbo: Nke afụ onye adịghị afụ ibe.
proverbs.english: What one suffers is not what his fellow suffers.
proverbs.usage: A poor man cannot feed his children; a rich man has none to feed.

proverbs.igbo: Onye ọchụ gbuka mbada, mụ ụmụ anọ dị ibe.
proverbs.english: The hunter kills many duiker but his four children are pawned.
proverbs.usage: If a man complains that his share is small when he has not made a title.

proverbs.igbo: Isi anụ ka a na-afụ anya ya.
proverbs.english: In the head of an animal they find its eyes.
proverbs.usage: One in need goes to a rich man.

proverbs.igbo: Dị ka ogbenye, ọgụ ọjọọ ka ọ na-alụ.
proverbs.english: So a poor man fights a bad fight, that is, with sticks, not money.

proverbs.igbo: Ala adịghị ekpokọ egbu onye n'ihi ntụtụ isi ya dị elu.
proverbs.english: The town does not gather to kill one because his hair is long.
proverbs.usage: A rich man stays at home when he has palaver with another town; poor people go and die.

proverbs.igbo: Ọhịa enyi na-abanye, mgbada na-abanyekwa n'ime.
proverbs.english: The bush elephant walks in, the duiker also walks in.
proverbs.usage: Rich and poor can both use the road.

proverbs.igbo: Nwoke adịghị oke na anụ kpuchie mbọ ya.
proverbs.english: A man is not so stout that flesh covers his nails.
proverbs.usage: No one is so rich that someone does not own him.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụ na ka ha gbusi nwa dibịa ka ha gbusi nwa ofeke?
proverbs.english: They don't kill the child of a doctor and an ignoramus the same way.
proverbs.usage: Rich and poor get different treatment.

proverbs.igbo: Onye arịrịọ enweghị ihere.
proverbs.english: A beggar has no shame.

proverbs.igbo: Ụzọ ego adịghị mfe.
proverbs.english: Getting money is not easy.

proverbs.igbo: Ogbenye na-ekwu okwu ka ọ dị ọrịa.
proverbs.english: A poor man talks as if he were not well.

proverbs.igbo: Onye eji dị n'olu amaghị na ọ na-eke ụcha.
proverbs.english: He who has beads on his neck does not know that it shows its colour.
proverbs.usage: If a rich man's son steals.

proverbs.igbo: Nwa mazi dị n'afọ bụ ọgbọ nwa ogbenye.
proverbs.english: The son of a rich man in the womb is the same age as a poor man's son.
proverbs.usage: A rich man's son is above a poor man who is older.

proverbs.igbo: Nwa nze dị afọ bụ nwanne ogbenye gbụọ.
proverbs.english: The son of a rich man in the womb is the companion of a poor man.
proverbs.usage: A rich man's son has advantages.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ na-atụkọ tụkọ, adịghị atụ nke nne n'ahịa.
proverbs.english: He can distinguish footsteps well, he cannot distinguish his mother's in the market.
proverbs.usage: The son of a rich man does not know how his father became rich.

proverbs.igbo: Ewu adịghị ata igu, ata ekwele.
proverbs.english: A goat does not bite palm leaves and bite ekwele (tie-tie) at once.
proverbs.usage: A poor man's child cannot leave its father and go to a rich man.

proverbs.igbo: Ụwa dị iche iche.
proverbs.english: The world is varied.
proverbs.usage: A woman may be rich and good-looking but have no children.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ dịghị onye na-atụgharị ihu karịa onye anwụrụ ọkụ na-egbu.
proverbs.english: No one turns his face more than the one that smoke hurts.
proverbs.usage: One who has means of livelihood is better off than one who has none.

proverbs.igbo: Onye mgba adịghị agba na onye nwe ụlọ.
proverbs.english: A wrestler does not wrestle with the owner (father) of the house.
proverbs.usage: A man must not quarrel with his master.

proverbs.igbo: Ụwa bụ otu a.
proverbs.english: The world is this (such is life).
proverbs.usage: When a man finds servants neglecting their work.

proverbs.igbo: Ọzọ bụ aba; dibịa na-asa ya.
proverbs.english: A blacksmith makes a staple; the doctor washes it.
proverbs.usage: Of a man who boasts of knowing more than his master.

proverbs.igbo: Odibo abụ eze bụ eze ọfụma; odibo bụa eze n'abụọ, ọ lịe.
proverbs.english: A servant serves a king, he serves the king well; a servant serves two kings, he is true to one.

proverbs.igbo: Agene adaghị n'elu akpọ Lokọja.
proverbs.english: A native mat never lies on a Lokoja mat; a man is less than his master.

proverbs.igbo: Onye nwe egede kpọpụọ ya, ọ dịghị ajọ njọ.
proverbs.english: Who has a drum and bursts it, it is not bad; an owner is not blamed.

proverbs.igbo: Ụbọchị onye nwe ụlọ tiwara ụkọ, ka oge eruzu; nwata tiwara ya, a kụọ ya ihe.
proverbs.english: The day the owner of a house breaks a calabash, its time has come; a child breaks it, they flog him; an owner is not blamed.

proverbs.igbo: Onye nwe ike ịti aka.
proverbs.english: Who has buttocks can slap them; an owner is not blamed.

proverbs.igbo: Nkịta adịghị abọ n'ebe onye nwe ya.
proverbs.english: A dog does not bark at his master.

proverbs.igbo: Onye mụtara adịghị aka onye nkuzi.
proverbs.english: A learner is not greater than his teacher.

proverbs.igbo: A dịghị ama ihe ha na-asị ọgọ.
proverbs.english: They don't know what they say to a relative-in-law.
proverbs.usage: Go slow with your superior.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụghị na osisi nwere ọtụtụ akọtụ ka ọ na-amị ihe a na-eri.
proverbs.english: It is not because a tree has many roots that it bears a thing they eat.
proverbs.usage: Inferiors stand when a superior comes, even if he is a small man.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ ka onye, a na-enye ya ola.
proverbs.english: He surpasses one and forces old food (yesterday's) on him.

proverbs.igbo: Ọgọ adịghị egbu ọgọ, anyị amaghị onye ha gbanyere ya.
proverbs.english: A father-in-law does not kill his son-in-law; we don't know for whom they forbid it.
proverbs.usage: Son-in-law does not inform against father-in-law.

proverbs.igbo: Osisi na-asị ala na ọ dị ochie, anyị amaghị ebe ọ si pụta.
proverbs.english: A tree that says to the ground he is older, we don't know where it grows from.
proverbs.usage: When a child rebukes his father.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụghị na ara wakpọrọ, ka ọ na-ada.
proverbs.english: It is not the day breasts develop that they fall.
proverbs.usage: When children advise parents.

proverbs.igbo: Ibudu adịghị ada nọ n'elu.
proverbs.english: A trap on the ground cannot fall on an animal if it is in a tree; a boy cannot know more than his father.

proverbs.igbo: Ha adịghị agụ akwa ọkụkọ amụ ọkpa.
proverbs.english: They never consider an egg to know the cock; a child does not know more than his father.

proverbs.igbo: Mmiri adịghị aka onye nwe ụlọ amụ ihe.
proverbs.english: Rain does not know better than the householder; a child is not wiser than its father.

proverbs.igbo: Ege dị okpo adịghị mma ibu aja; ọ bụ isi ga-ebu ya.
proverbs.english: The flower of okpo is not good for carrying sacrifice; it is the head that will carry it.
proverbs.usage: When a son asks his father to buy a wife, when he has no money.

proverbs.igbo: Ọdịda adịghị ewepụ ihe dị n'afọ; onye dara ebulu nke ya bili ọtọ.
proverbs.english: Falling does not throw away things in the stomach; who falls takes up his and stands up.
proverbs.usage: (a) If a child speaks without being asked. (b) Strangers don't understand each other as friends do.

proverbs.igbo: Aka nri ka eji eti nwa; aka ekpe ka eji adụ n'anya.
proverbs.english: The right hand they take to beat a child; the left they take to caress.
proverbs.usage: An enemy may say "flog," but he does not replace a dead child.

proverbs.igbo: Mgbe nna m dị ndụ, anyị adaghị ahụ nsogbu; nna bụ chi onye.
proverbs.english: When my father was alive, we did not see trouble; a father is a man's chi.
proverbs.usage: The son suffers when his father dies.

proverbs.igbo: Onye nwere nwa jọrọ njọ agaghị ewe okpokoro gbuo ya.
proverbs.english: He who has a bad child cannot take wood to kill him.
proverbs.usage: When people complain to a father of his child.

proverbs.igbo: Ha adịghị eji isi awọ amụ ihe.
proverbs.english: They do not take grey hair to know something.
proverbs.usage: (a) If a child learns much from father and grows wise in youth. (b) Elders must consult younger men also. Cf. 520.

proverbs.igbo: Yamwa abụghị aha, nwa Ojei nwere iwe, wee gọọ aha.
proverbs.english: Yamwa is not a name; the son of Ojei was angry and gave the name.
proverbs.usage: When a man's sons all die, the father refuses to name another.

proverbs.igbo: Anya na-aga n'ụzọ mmụọ na-eche onye nwe ya.
proverbs.english: Eyes that go off wait for their owner on the spirit road.
proverbs.usage: To a woman that loses her child.

proverbs.igbo: Emume anaghị eji ịrụ ụkwụ apụ.
proverbs.english: Trouble does not go away by shaking the leg.
proverbs.usage: When a man worries his parents to buy things instead of working.

proverbs.igbo: Eneke m ọbịa, sie nye ya nri.
proverbs.english: To entertain a stranger, you cook and give him food.
proverbs.usage: To a son-in-law who does not serve his father-in-law properly.

proverbs.igbo: Ire mele, nwa atụrụ.
proverbs.english: Tongue did it; Ilemele is a child of sheep.
proverbs.usage: Ilemele was caught by ubido (tiger cat) because she would not keep silence at her mother's orders; used when a second in line, seeing a find on the road, makes it his own before the first can pick it up by saying 'abụ m.'

proverbs.igbo: A na-ato ilu, a naghị echefu ọnwụ.
proverbs.english: They do not speak a proverb and forget death.
proverbs.usage: A child does not forget his father's last words.

proverbs.igbo: Oyi na-atụ ihe, ọgọlọ nwanne ya na-atụ ihe.
proverbs.english: A cold catches differently; harmattan, its brother, catches differently.
proverbs.usage: A man's children are not all the same.

proverbs.igbo: Nwata nọ n'ụzọ na-akọcha onye na-aga ije; na-atụkwasị obi na nna ya nọ nso.
proverbs.english: A child stands by the way and abuses passers-by; he trusts that his father is near.

proverbs.igbo: Otu nwa amaka n'ụbọchị egwu; ọ bụrụ na nsogbu bịara, ọ na-akwa.
proverbs.english: One child is good on the day of a dance; when trouble comes he cries.
proverbs.usage: A man wants all good things for his child; in the day of trouble he can bear it alone.

proverbs.igbo: Ihe a naghị ahụ n'ọrị nne ewu, a naghị ahụ n'ọrị nwa.
proverbs.english: Things not seen in the vulva of the goat, they will not see in that of the child.
proverbs.usage: The son will not accept treatment his father would not allow.

proverbs.igbo: Oke adịghị eji ọdụ etiwa ite
proverbs.english: A rat does not take its tail to break a pot.
proverbs.usage: A child cannot cohabit with its mother.

proverbs.igbo: Nwata amaghị ụbọchị a mụrụ nne ya
proverbs.english: A child does not know the day his mother was born.
proverbs.usage: A child cannot act ill to his mother's people, because he may have to run to them.

proverbs.igbo: Agwọ pịa nwa ya, sị ha, weta nwa agwọ ahịhịa ka ha gbue
proverbs.english: The snake bites its child, says to them: bring the child of a grass snake to kill.
proverbs.usage: When A hides the misdeeds of his own child and exposes those of B's.

proverbs.igbo: Ife ha ji agọ nwa ka ha ji agọ nwa, ha adịghị eji ọtọ agọ nwa
proverbs.english: What they take to coax a child, they take; they never take a woman's genitals to coax a child.
proverbs.usage: Husband to wife: don't praise a bad son.

proverbs.igbo: Nne mbe na-ebu okpokoro, nwa ebulu na-ebu ajị
proverbs.english: The mother of the tortoise wears a shell and her child wears hair.
proverbs.usage: A child cannot say to his father that he copulates with more women than his father, including his mother.

proverbs.igbo: Nkpo dị n'ife, ma ọ dịghị n'ife; ọ na-akọ n'anya ọkụ
proverbs.english: A round basket is useful or useless; it hangs over the fire.
proverbs.usage: A man must not drive his family out.

proverbs.igbo: Ozi onye na-abụ, ka e ji agụ eyi.
proverbs.english: Who teaches singing is imitated; a family imitates its head.

proverbs.igbo: Abụlụ aka ọdọ, abụlụ nne.
proverbs.english: If you take the mortar, take the pestle; if a wife is taken by force, take the child too.

proverbs.igbo: Etete n'aka bụ ụwa.
proverbs.english: Softly and careful is the world.
proverbs.usage: To rebuke wild children.

proverbs.igbo: Chibụọzọ sị ewụ mmadụ na-akwa m, ma nke ya sị nyem akpụji.
proverbs.english: Chibụọzọ says other people's goat cries at me, but his own says give me seed yam.
proverbs.usage: When a man's own family are backward and unorderly.

proverbs.igbo: Nwayọ bụ ije.
proverbs.english: Slow and sure.
proverbs.usage: To a child that is in a hurry or violent.

proverbs.igbo: Ọlọlọbwọ sị nwata ya, Egbukwena ya, n'afọ atọ ka i jaa.
proverbs.english: Ọlọlọbwọ says to his child, do not kill me, for three years you take to cut him up.
proverbs.usage: Warning to a child not to violate customs.

proverbs.igbo: Ịbụ ibu ka mmadụ agwa nwa ya na-aga gafee obodo.
proverbs.english: If you get trouble you carry it, as a man said to his son who was going out in the town.
proverbs.usage: Warning to child.

proverbs.igbo: Ọkụlọ adịghị asọ onye kọrọ ya.
proverbs.english: Ọkụlọ does not grow bigger than the planter.
proverbs.usage: Warning to child.

proverbs.igbo: A kpọkọ ụlọ, a hụwa nkọ.
proverbs.english: If they unroof a house, they see wood.
proverbs.usage: If a man plants yams but does not weed, he gets no yams.

proverbs.igbo: Otu isi anaghị ahụ ụzọ nri ụtụtụ; ọ dị ka ọbụ atala (akpịrị).
proverbs.english: One head does not see the road to breakfast; it is like economising.
proverbs.usage: When a man takes no one with him to farm.

proverbs.igbo: Ọkpa e ji aga ubi adịghị aka nwa ji.
proverbs.english: A basket they take to farm never comes back without small yams.

proverbs.igbo: Mụ na ha jiri igwe, ọ dị ka anyị nọ n'otu.
proverbs.english: I and they work together, it is as though we are all one.
proverbs.usage: A solitary man who sees a crowd at work.

proverbs.igbo: Mmadụ adịghị akọ ntutu isi ya.
proverbs.english: A man does not shave his own hair.
proverbs.usage: When a man asks ebo to go with him to work and they cry off.

proverbs.igbo: Akụ agwụghị, agba agaghị ezu ike.
proverbs.english: If the kernels are not finished, the jaw will not rest.
proverbs.usage: A man must finish his work.

proverbs.igbo: Ọnwụ gburu onye na-egbu mmadụ; nke na-ele anya na-asị na ya ga-ata ọka ọtụmị.
proverbs.english: Death kills one that sacrifices a person; one who looks on says he will live (bite corn) longer.
proverbs.usage: By a man who gives up work.

proverbs.igbo: Nkwụ daa, ọkà atọpụ.
proverbs.english: Palm tree falls, younger one comes up.
proverbs.usage: To encourage one who finds his work hard; all labour has an end.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụ ọbụwa jiri onwe ya n'anwụ.
proverbs.english: Who hoes, stands in the sun.
proverbs.usage: When a worker has not finished with his fellows.

proverbs.igbo: Ife onye na-arụ bụ ubi ya.
proverbs.english: What one does is his farm.
proverbs.usage: Every one has his own work.

proverbs.igbo: Ogo na-ayo ọrụ, di na-ayo ọrụ.
proverbs.english: Father-in-law asks for work, husband asks for work.

proverbs.igbo: Ene na-eri ọkụrọ, ọ na-aga iburu ọgwụ ọkụrị.
proverbs.english: Bush buck eats okro, goes to get medicine for dry cough.
proverbs.usage: Workman must look to his tools.

proverbs.igbo: Nwa gburu onye, nwa ka a ga-amụkwa.
proverbs.english: A child kills one, a child they will bear.
proverbs.usage: If a man is killed at work, others do the same work, e.g. climbing.

proverbs.igbo: Ịbara mkpu adịbeghị amamihe, ife uzu.
proverbs.english: Those who run out at a shout are not the wiser ones.
proverbs.usage: One who has work to do begins before helpers come.

proverbs.igbo: Ha adịghị ebu ebi aga ịgba afa n'ala.
proverbs.english: They do not carry elephantiasis to divine on the ground.
proverbs.usage: When a busy man is called for other work.

proverbs.igbo: Oti akị ti akị, nke bu ọkịele abịa n'ọbụ.
proverbs.english: Who breaks nut, breaks nut, who gathers shells has fame.
proverbs.usage: Refusing to do another man's work.

proverbs.igbo: Anụ na-amụgharị anaghị abanye n'ọnya.
proverbs.english: An animal that trembles does not walk into a trap.
proverbs.usage: One who works becomes rich.

proverbs.igbo: Ọkịkọ bụ ọrụ, ịkwa bụ ọrụ. Ọrụ bụ ọrụ.
proverbs.english: Tying the sticks on the roof is work, patching is work; work is work.

proverbs.igbo: Ha ziri ọkà bịa gbaa; ọ sị na ya amaghị agba.
proverbs.english: They send to the hunter to come and shoot; he says he does not know how.
proverbs.usage: When a man sent for to do work cannot do it.

proverbs.igbo: Azịza abụghị ihe; n'ụtụtụ ha na-achọ azịza, ọ dịghị.
proverbs.english: A broom is nothing; in the morning they go about looking for a broom.
proverbs.usage: When a worker is sent for after a man has said he is worthless.

proverbs.igbo: Amasị ịwata ọkụ, dọseni ọkọ, ọ sị na agụ na-agụ ya.
proverbs.english: They don't say to a child 'make fire'; and he says he is hungry.
proverbs.usage: A man does not provide food till work is done.

proverbs.igbo: Ha eli, afọ ọ pụta.
proverbs.english: When they eat, the belly comes out.
proverbs.usage: A man calls people to work, and feeds them; then they work.

proverbs.igbo: Ha adịghị eji afọ ọkọ ata ụfọlị.
proverbs.english: They never take spice with empty belly.
proverbs.usage: If someone asks a man to work without preparing food.

proverbs.igbo: Ọbọ butere mbibi na ntịkọ.
proverbs.english: Laziness brings spoiling and destruction.

proverbs.igbo: Afọ jee, ka ọ bịa, adịghị efele n'ọnụ.
proverbs.english: The year goes, let it come; it is not hard (scarce) to a lazy man in his mouth.

proverbs.igbo: Nkpụlọobi onye ọbọ na-achọ, ma o nweghị ihe.
proverbs.english: The heart of a lazy man desires and has nothing.

proverbs.igbo: Nke onye nwere, ibe enweghị; ijiji jị akwa, ngwele bụ ọtọ.
proverbs.english: What one has, another has not; the fly has a cloth; the lizard is naked.
proverbs.usage: A lazy man may prosper.

proverbs.igbo: Uzere enyere ụkwara aka.
proverbs.english: Sneezing assists the cough.
proverbs.usage: A lazy man makes excuses — I can't go to farm; there is work in the town.

proverbs.igbo: Ubi tụrụ ime, ọ dị efele ka ọ weli.
proverbs.english: The farm produces (conceives); it is the lazy man that takes them.
proverbs.usage: Said to a lazy man.

proverbs.igbo: Udene adịghị eje ahịa ụra; udene zụta ihe, ọ na-ala.
proverbs.english: The vulture does not go to market to sleep; the vulture buys and goes.
proverbs.usage: Don't waste morning.

proverbs.igbo: Ilo si na nwata bọọ ije, ya bọọ ọlu.
proverbs.english: The nightjar says that a boy runs after it; it stops him from working.
proverbs.usage: If a boy plays instead of working in the farm, he gets still more work.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụsi onye ji agụ igụ, anaghị efu n'ihi mwakọ na-egbu ihe bụ.
proverbs.english: The day one takes to look for a louse, he does not lose because he looks for things that kill him.
proverbs.usage: When a farmer hunts pig instead of working.

proverbs.igbo: Nwata riri isi nnụnụ, ọ gaa uji.
proverbs.english: A child eats the head of a bird, he goes to uji (hole in tree, where birds come for water, i.e., tries to shoot them).
proverbs.usage: To an idle busybody who changes his ways.

proverbs.igbo: Aka arụ, ọ na-ọlị.
proverbs.english: The hand tells when to leave work. Fatigue, not the hour, decides a man to stop.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ dịla onye mma, gịnị k'ọ ga-egbu gaa be dibia?
proverbs.english: If it is well with one, why does he go to the doctor's house?

proverbs.igbo: Onye bu akpọnụ adaghị ebu ntọkẹ.
proverbs.english: One who has goitre does not wear small beads (coral).

proverbs.igbo: Onye na-eje nwayọ na-agba ọsọ.
proverbs.english: A quiet goer runs fast (i.e., does much harm).
proverbs.usage: Of a quiet man.

proverbs.igbo: Ka onye si je, ka e bu ya.
proverbs.english: As one's rank, so they give seat. As one's appearance, so they give seat.

proverbs.igbo: Omume onye bụ mma.
proverbs.english: A man's deeds are his 'beauty.'
proverbs.usage: When a girl refuses one man and chooses a worse-looking one.

proverbs.igbo: Anaghị anọ n'azụ ụlọ akọ ụlọ mma.
proverbs.english: They never stay behind the house and say the house is good. Appearances are deceptive.

proverbs.igbo: Ujuju adị aka mma n'isi anyịike, ma ọ mụwa, ọ taa.
proverbs.english: The tree is very good for the head of the axe, but it will not last. Appearances are deceptive; chance acquaintance may be poor.

proverbs.igbo: A naghị eji isi awọ eke ubi.
proverbs.english: They never take plots in farm by grey hair. A thin man may have a big farm.

proverbs.igbo: Kpakpa tụrụ ọkọ, nwa mara mma kọdị n'enu, ọ dana n'ani ịcha akpụ.
proverbs.english: The cotton tree flower is fine when it is up, it falls as a nut. A young woman is fine, an old woman withered.

proverbs.igbo: Ozugunzugu si na onye obụ ihe nkiti, n'anya adịghị n'onye fụ mma.
proverbs.english: Owl says who kept silence; the eye of that one is not good.
proverbs.usage: Wrongdoer injures man who says nothing; next time injured man threatens revenge.

proverbs.igbo: Onye anya mpi kwuru okwu mbụ, kwuru abụọ; asị ya, tụpị anya gị nọọ n'osọ.
proverbs.english: Half blind man (blind of one eye) spoke once, spoke twice; they say to him: close your eyes and go aside.
proverbs.usage: Injured man says this. If a man injures another twice without apology, he pays penalty.

proverbs.igbo: Ọfị adịghị egbu nwa, fanye ya afịa nne ya ịja afịa.
proverbs.english: White yaws does not kill a child, they take it to flatter the mother.
proverbs.usage: To console man in trouble.

proverbs.igbo: Ije a dị; ka m kee kwu zi?
proverbs.english: (Let) the journey (be) so; what am I to say?
proverbs.usage: When a man comes from court and says he has been heavily fined.

proverbs.igbo: Iyi adịghị eri mbabọ isi.
proverbs.english: The river does not eat a blind calabash (i.e., an unbroken one).

proverbs.igbo: Nwata bụ enyi okenye, n'okwu erughị ya.
proverbs.english: If a child is the friend of an old man, palaver does not meet him.
proverbs.usage: But he must not trust to it; when palaver comes, he is forsaken.

proverbs.igbo: Okopụ mwaka bụ eze ọrịa.
proverbs.english: Downcast is king of illness.
proverbs.usage: To cheer up in misfortune.

proverbs.igbo: Otu nne dị iche.
proverbs.english: One's own brother is different.
proverbs.usage: A man standing alone is weak.

proverbs.igbo: Otu onye jee ije, ọdụdụ ata ya.
proverbs.english: One man goes alone, tsetse kills him.
proverbs.usage: There is safety in numbers.

proverbs.igbo: Ọba sị, nwụrụ ala onye ọwa fụnere ya n'ala Idụ.
proverbs.english: The king says find for him one who is a failure in the land of Idú.
proverbs.usage: One who sees another in need and tries to help.

proverbs.igbo: Ọsa bute, ọ bute n'ụze; ụze bute, ọ bute n'ọsa.
proverbs.english: Osa fetches, fetches for Uze; Uze fetches for Osa (Osa and Uze are species of squirrels).
proverbs.usage: Brothers help each other.

proverbs.igbo: Alọlọ bụ ike ji; ji na-enweghị alọlọ agbaghị elu.
proverbs.english: A small yam stick is the strength of the yam; without alolo it does not climb.
proverbs.usage: Of a man who has no supporter.

proverbs.igbo: Nwata gbue ọlọbwe; ọ hụghị ọkụ o ji ria ya.
proverbs.english: A child kills a boa; it does not see fire to roast it.
proverbs.usage: When a man can't find a helper.

proverbs.igbo: Osoko je be Ogwoko.
proverbs.english: Osoko goes to Ogwoko (helpless runs to helpless).
proverbs.usage: When a man with a palaver gets a useless backer.

proverbs.igbo: Àdàkada sị n'ugwu: Ọ kụkụ ka ị na-akwụ ibu, ka ị na-ebu? Ọ na-ana ya, ka ị na-ana ya?
proverbs.english: The dung beetle says to the hill: are you helping him with his load or do you take it from him?
proverbs.usage: To a false friend in a palaver.

proverbs.igbo: Ka anyị na-ele ụwa.
proverbs.english: Look at the world.
proverbs.usage: Consolation for misfortune.

proverbs.igbo: A kụrụ akpụ maka ụnwụ; ụnwụ anwụ, akpụ a bịa.
proverbs.english: They plant pumpkin for a famine; the famine goes, pumpkin begins to bear.
proverbs.usage: If the trusted helper fails.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụrụ na mmiri taa, ọ na-eru n'obi.
proverbs.english: Even if the river dries much it reaches (catches) the chest.
proverbs.usage: Consolation; "you have suffered all and cannot suffer more."

proverbs.igbo: Onye mere ya, ya dị ya.
proverbs.english: Let him bear it, to whom it happens.
proverbs.usage: To a man who laments his losses (he must bear up).

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụrụ na ụnwụ akawaa, anyasị ka ụnwụ ji ala.
proverbs.english: However big the famine, in the evening famine takes a small yam.
proverbs.usage: Even after big losses we eat.

proverbs.igbo: Ọnwụ agụka na-akọ anyasị
proverbs.english: Famine satisfaction comes in the evening (to a hungry child).

proverbs.igbo: A sị m bụrụ nwoke, m ga-eso gị abụọ
proverbs.english: If I had been a man, I would have made you two (i.e. accompanied you).
proverbs.usage: Sister to brotherless man.

proverbs.igbo: Chi mmadụ dị abụọ
proverbs.english: A man's chi are two.
proverbs.usage: A doctor is like a man's chi; said if a man saves a boy from a big man.

proverbs.igbo: Abụzị na-akwa n'ikpere anyasị, ọ na-abanye n'ime olulu, ọ maghị na chi agwụla
proverbs.english: A cricket cries, in the evening it goes into a hole, it does not know that the night is far gone.
proverbs.usage: A prudent man lays up for a rainy day.

proverbs.igbo: A sị m ma adịghị ebute ụzọ, n'azụ ka ọ na-abịa
proverbs.english: "If I had known" does not come first but last; prudence comes after the event.

proverbs.igbo: Nwata amaghị ụwa, ọ na-aja ji n'ọmẹ
proverbs.english: A child does not know the world, he praises a yam in shoots (half-grown).
proverbs.usage: Examine before you praise.

proverbs.igbo: Ajọ nrọ adịghị eketu mmadụ n'ụlọ mụọ
proverbs.english: A bad dream never leaves a man in the house of the mụọ.
proverbs.usage: By a man who retires from matter to avoid ill consequences.

proverbs.igbo: Adịghị asa nke ọma karịa onye jere iyi
proverbs.english: They never wash better than the one who went to the river.
proverbs.usage: If a cook complains of not getting enough food.

proverbs.igbo: Arụrụ na-eso ogwe gafee iyi.
proverbs.english: Insects follow a log to cross a river.
proverbs.usage: A man takes a guide to unknown places.

proverbs.igbo: Onye Ọka sị n'anya, ma jị mba, na ọ lụọ Ọka.
proverbs.english: The craftsman who does favours gets no money.

proverbs.igbo: Ọmọtụ gbọọ anya.
proverbs.english: A strong child that has no sense.
proverbs.usage: To a violent man, or foolish.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ rọọ nrọ kwụ n'ụlọ, edina nrọ n'ụlọ.
proverbs.english: Standing dreamt, lying down dreamt.
proverbs.usage: It is no use losing one's temper because a thing is not done, if one has not taken thought before.

proverbs.igbo: Onye jekwuru akwa, ya laa anya, ọ ga-eji gịnị akwa?
proverbs.english: If a man who is going to cry loses his eyes, what will he cry with?
proverbs.usage: If a person does not prepare.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụrụ na anyị aga n'ubi iri nri, anyị ga-ewe anwụrụ.
proverbs.english: If we had gone to the farm to eat we should take smoke.
proverbs.usage: If a person does not prepare.

proverbs.igbo: Ụbọchị erubeghị, a naghị akọ ya ọjọọ.
proverbs.english: Day not done, they don't say it is not good (or bad).

proverbs.igbo: Anyị amaghị okwu, anyị atụ isi tinye.
proverbs.english: We will not help one to speak and lose our heads.

proverbs.igbo: Onye ngwụrọ na-arịọ ibe ji abụọ ka o ru aka
proverbs.english: Lame man asks for two slices of yam that one may reach him.
proverbs.usage: When a man begs for more than he wants to make sure of getting something.

proverbs.igbo: Ilolo bụ ike
proverbs.english: Taking thought is strength.
proverbs.usage: To a man who has hard work to live.

proverbs.igbo: Ije k'obi ọ ma ihe ọ ga-agwa obi; ọ mazị ihe obi ga-agwa ya
proverbs.english: Who goes to obi knows the thing he will say to obi; he does not know what obi will say to him when he goes to him.
proverbs.usage: When a man gets farm land, they say 'take plenty'; he does not, and finds the land is good.

proverbs.igbo: Anwụ lamalama na-eli ji
proverbs.english: The sun shines a little and eats yams; a stitch in time saves nine.

proverbs.igbo: Onye gbúrú agụ zị onwe ya Idu
proverbs.english: One who kills a leopard sends himself to Idu (the leopard was formerly sent to Oba Idu); a thief counts his punishment.

proverbs.igbo: Mmadụ amaghị ebe ọ ga-ata ọjị
proverbs.english: A man does not know how long he has to live.
proverbs.usage: If a man refuses to plant kola, he thinks he will not eat of it.

proverbs.igbo: Inyi adịghị egbu ọgwụ egbu onye so ya
proverbs.english: Inyi tree does not kill witch and kill who accompanies him.
proverbs.usage: By a man who retires from a matter to avoid ill consequences.

proverbs.igbo: Ọnya adị anwụ agwọ
proverbs.english: A trap does not catch a snake.
proverbs.usage: If a person escapes his enemies.

proverbs.igbo: A naghị agwa nwa ozu na ọ naghị eli ozu nke ọma, maka na ọ bụ nke mbụ.
proverbs.english: They don't tell a child of a dead man that he does not bury well, because it is the first burial.

proverbs.igbo: Ngwele elu da n'ani, sị madụ adịghị eja ya, ya jaa onwe ya.
proverbs.english: A lizard falls down from above; it says people do not praise it, it praises itself.
proverbs.usage: When work is well done and is not praised by the recipient.

proverbs.igbo: Oke bụ igwe n'ebo.
proverbs.english: The old (big) man is the benefactor of the ebo.
proverbs.usage: An ebo is badly off without a wise man.

proverbs.igbo: Ụzọ dị jụụ, nduru ebu opi.
proverbs.english: If the road is quiet, a dove blows a long flute.
proverbs.usage: When a man asks advice, he waits till the councillor is disengaged.

proverbs.igbo: Madụ alala nne.
proverbs.english: If someone advises a man to wash his sore harder.

proverbs.igbo: Ike gwụrụ, ọnwụ bịa, esizi ike.
proverbs.english: The fighter stops fighting when death comes.
proverbs.usage: When a strong man commits murder and is hanged (he has been warned in these terms).

proverbs.igbo: Kube ofe sie.
proverbs.english: Take soup and boil.
proverbs.usage: A strong man kills people; they use this proverb to advise him to stop.

proverbs.igbo: Onye kpọrọ ọnya, ọ na-ahịa ji.
proverbs.english: One who has set a trap roasts yams and eats.
proverbs.usage: Warning to a man who sleeps away from home without reason (e.g., goes visiting in town).

proverbs.igbo: Ịta bụ nri ntị.
proverbs.english: Tales are the food of the ear.
proverbs.usage: To persuade an unwilling person to come.

proverbs.igbo: Ọmata kwuru onye ọnụ, mbịa ya erighị.
proverbs.english: If a good man meets a talkative one, his coming is useless.
proverbs.usage: Of a man who traduces.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụ n'Ezomo onye ga-ebu Ọdịa?
proverbs.english: If not Ezomo, who would have borne Odia.
proverbs.usage: To a man who complains that Onirhe has done something to him.

proverbs.igbo: Elu na-eche.
proverbs.english: The world thinks.
proverbs.usage: When a man abuses another in the presence of others.

proverbs.igbo: Okwu n'azụ onye ya pụta ihu m, kwuo.
proverbs.english: Let a backbiter come to my face and speak.

proverbs.igbo: Efi nwere nne bụ obolo.
proverbs.english: A cow that has a mother is a heifer (not old).
proverbs.usage: When someone abuses one older than himself.

proverbs.igbo: Nnọkọ ọnụ na-ebute ọkà.
proverbs.english: Sitting together causes backbiting.
proverbs.usage: If a newcomer joins a party and tells lies in order to join them.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ na-atamụ ka ogbome.
proverbs.english: He speaks ill like a wizard (who is on bad terms with all).

proverbs.igbo: Onye asị na-ege ntị ire jọ, ọ bụ onye.
proverbs.english: A liar listens to a bad tongue.

proverbs.igbo: Ọkụkọ rịta ibe ji abụọ na-akwa akwa na ọ dịghị ya eze; ewu nwere eze, olee izi ọ na-eri?
proverbs.english: A fowl eats two slices of yam and complains he has no teeth; a goat that has teeth, how many does it eat?
proverbs.usage: Don't look a gift horse in the mouth.

proverbs.igbo: E were ododo kpaa abọ, abọ ka ọ bụ.
proverbs.english: They take a red cloth to make a long basket and it is a basket still.
proverbs.usage: It is waste to do a kindness to the ungrateful.

proverbs.igbo: Nwata kweere ọrụ, nke ya na-eche ya.
proverbs.english: A child agrees to work, his own waits for him.
proverbs.usage: A kind-hearted person reaps ingratitude.

proverbs.igbo: Ebu m, ọnya m ebu; nke m gburu ekweghị m ịhụ nkpụ.
proverbs.english: I kill, my trap kills; what I kill does not allow me to see my catch.
proverbs.usage: When a man is ungrateful for father's help.

proverbs.igbo: Onye mere ọgaranya, ọ na-echefu onye na-eche ya mgbe ọ bụ ogbenye.
proverbs.english: When one becomes rich, he forgets one that keeps to him when he was poor.
proverbs.usage: Ingratitude.

proverbs.igbo: Atụ aka, aka mụọ ihe; atụ aka ọ bọdị, ọ fụọ aka.
proverbs.english: If a man who receives help is ungrateful, he gets no help again.

proverbs.igbo: Ọkụkọ adịghị echefu onye dọpụrụ ọdụ ya n'oge udu mmiri.
proverbs.english: A fowl does not forget who pulls out his tail in a rainy season.
proverbs.usage: Gratitude.

proverbs.igbo: Nkụjị mị ya ka abụọ ji kuru obogulu na ubi.
proverbs.english: Leading out (bears it) makes calabash take pumpkin to the farm.
proverbs.usage: When a man forgets his benefactor through selfishness; anger.

proverbs.igbo: Ifejioku adịghị egbu dị n'ubi, ma ọ na-aga.
proverbs.english: Ifejioku does not kill the farmer in his farm, because he goes (to other farm).
proverbs.usage: When a man says too much he lies.

proverbs.igbo: Ha adịghị eji iwe egbu nwa mma.
proverbs.english: They don't take vexation to kill small knife.

proverbs.igbo: Iwe na-akpọ nwa ọfụ kee akwa; ebe ọfụ adịghị eji akwa n'ọhịa.
proverbs.english: Anger leads "fox" to tie cloth; the country of "fox" does not wear cloth in the bush.
proverbs.usage: When a man acts in anger.

proverbs.igbo: Nwata rie ife gbawara afọ, o were afọ buru uzọ.
proverbs.english: If a child eats something that bursts belly, he puts belly before him.
proverbs.usage: A man who causes trouble must bear it.

proverbs.igbo: Ife onye kọrọ, ọ kwọrọ ya.
proverbs.english: What one sows, he reaps (bear for him).

proverbs.igbo: Ọnwụ egbughị iwokete, ọ mesịa ọ bụrụ ka nne nkwụ.
proverbs.english: If death does not kill a young palm, afterwards it becomes a big palm.
proverbs.usage: If a big boy beats a small boy; he can pay out later.

proverbs.igbo: Nta wemere gọọ ife awobi; ma ọ bụna o ruo ụlọ, ọ gwa nwanne.
proverbs.english: They would have treated a worthless man foolishly, but if he reaches home, he tells his brothers.
proverbs.usage: A man takes money from his son-in-law; the son-in-law will get money for his daughters.

proverbs.igbo: Akwụkwọ asọsọ na-alụfụ nwa ewu
proverbs.english: A sweet leaf deceives a kid; a thief is caught sooner or later.

proverbs.igbo: Onye tụba n'ala, ọ tụba n'elu
proverbs.english: Who has much to do, has much to eat.

proverbs.igbo: Ụbụ ka n'ubu akpa, ma nkpo ka a na-akwụ
proverbs.english: We carry a bag on the shoulder but it is hung on a peg; a carrier must have rest.
proverbs.usage: Excuses and statements.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ jụm, m nwebe ebe m na-eri
proverbs.english: He is (I am) satisfied to have where he trusts that he stays to eat.
proverbs.usage: Of a man who is annoyed and refuses to eat (he has somewhere to eat).

proverbs.igbo: Ọkwa ọrụ gbaa, ha zaa ya
proverbs.english: A trumpeter calls for work, they answer him.
proverbs.usage: When a man excuses himself by saying he did not hear.

proverbs.igbo: Anụ m Nwambọ, amaghị m Nwambọ nke onye
proverbs.english: I heard of Nwambo, I don't know whose Nwambo it is.
proverbs.usage: By a witness who has nothing to say.

proverbs.igbo: Mmadụ adaghị onwe ya
proverbs.english: A person does not deny himself.
proverbs.usage: A man who fails is still the same man; he must not get a rich man to father him, and deny the name his father gave him.

proverbs.igbo: Ọkịni taka ita, ha atọọ ahịa
proverbs.english: Trader tells tales, they offer goods.
proverbs.usage: He says things are cheap, when they are dear.

proverbs.igbo: Anya ahụla ya
proverbs.english: The eyes of people have seen.
proverbs.usage: When a man denies.

proverbs.igbo: A mụ na m aka j'akpọ ọjụjụ, ọ jụ ụbọchị atọ
proverbs.english: If I knew the way to go to pick ojuju, it grows in three days.
proverbs.usage: To put off a man to whom one is going to do a favour later.

proverbs.igbo: Onye na-enweghị ego si na okwa asọghị ya
proverbs.english: One who has no money says that okwa does not please him.
proverbs.usage: Poor man cannot get a wife to cook his yams (sour grapes).

proverbs.igbo: Otu ọgọ ka ọ na-ama ọnya ilo
proverbs.english: False accusation pains more than a matchet wound.

proverbs.igbo: Ebe ọ lụ di ya, ọ na-egbu di ya, were nkpụkpọ tinye n'ọnụ
proverbs.english: Loved wife kills her husband, takes lamentation and puts it in her mouth.
proverbs.usage: She pretends.

proverbs.igbo: Azụ nwanyị adịghị akpọ okporo, ọ sịa: ka ya bịakwa
proverbs.english: Woman's latrine does not call woman, she says: wait a minute.
proverbs.usage: If a man calls, she makes no excuse.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụ eziokwu na ha gburu enyi, na ha buru isi ya lụọ ụlọ bụ asi
proverbs.english: (That) they killed the elephant is true, that they carried its head home is a lie.
proverbs.usage: Of a false accusation.

proverbs.igbo: Anya fụ Oloko ọjọ ihe
proverbs.english: Oloko met with something.
proverbs.usage: When a man is tired and wants to go.

proverbs.igbo: Ijiji ji akwa; ngwere bu akwa, ọ gba ọtọ.
proverbs.english: The fly ties a cloth; the lizard is big enough for a cloth, but goes naked.
proverbs.usage: When people are tired of a long meeting, carrying out one's plans.

proverbs.igbo: Aka nkpụnkpụ naara mbe ụzọ.
proverbs.english: A short hand takes away the tortoise's path.
proverbs.usage: When two people make a plan and one does not carry it out for want of money.

proverbs.igbo: Ọdịda na-ara ije n'azụ.
proverbs.english: Falling causes the journey to go back.

proverbs.igbo: Mmiri ka eze.
proverbs.english: Rain is more than the king.
proverbs.usage: The chief's orders cannot be carried out if natural causes prevent.

proverbs.igbo: Aka nkpụnkpụ ekweghị oke kpụọ ụzọ.
proverbs.english: A short hand does not let a rat cut a path.
proverbs.usage: When one does not carry out plans owing to illness.

proverbs.igbo: Isi eruteghị ebe ọ na-aga, ọ kwụsịghị.
proverbs.english: If the head does not reach the place it is going to, it does not stop.
proverbs.usage: Even if a man is hindered by others he fulfils his destiny.

proverbs.igbo: Onye na-ekwu na ya ga-eri nnukwu taa, na-atụkwasị ezé ya obi.
proverbs.english: One who says he will eat much more today trusts his teeth.

proverbs.igbo: Onye nta gburu enwe, bepụ ọdụ ya; ego ya ebelata.
proverbs.english: If a hunter kills a monkey and cuts off its tail, his money comes short.
proverbs.usage: When a man dies his plans come to nothing.

proverbs.igbo: Ọkụkọ abụọ zute udene, ha kpagburu ya.
proverbs.english: Two fowls meet a vulture, they choke him to death.
proverbs.usage: When men collect to do something they must do it well.

proverbs.igbo: Kosi si nne ya n'igbu gbue n'afà; ka ya nye ya nk'onye nwere nwa; ya ga-anwụ, e nye ya ka ọ si adị.
proverbs.english: Kosi says to mother: you kill him by name; let him bury her as one that has child; when he dies, they bury him as they like.
proverbs.usage: When a man cannot carry out a plan, he finishes as best he can.

proverbs.igbo: I banye n'ụlọ onye, a daghị ama àgwà ya.
proverbs.english: When you reach a man's house, his ways are not known.
proverbs.usage: When a man has been to a place of bad reputation (really good).

proverbs.igbo: Anaghị m anụ na Ukpebo etuwo tupu akwa m ... m erute.
proverbs.english: I can't hear that Ukpebo (a stream) rises much and loses cloth till I reach it (while I have not reached it).
proverbs.usage: Reputation does not frighten one from visiting a man.

proverbs.igbo: Omume onye bụ ndụ ya.
proverbs.english: A man's deeds are his life (good or bad).

proverbs.igbo: Anya adịghị ahụ ntị.
proverbs.english: The eye cannot see the ear.

proverbs.igbo: Onye oshi ma onye o zuru; ma onye o zuru amaghị.
proverbs.english: A thief knows the man from whom he steals; but the loser does not know (the thief).

proverbs.igbo: Ndị nzuzu na-akwa emo ndị amụma.
proverbs.english: Fools make a mock at prophets (visionaries).

proverbs.igbo: Ọgụmagana sị na ya dị okpoko; okpoko sị na ya dị ọgụmagana; ha abụọ na-ese okwu.
proverbs.english: Chameleon says he is older than the hornbill; hornbill says he is older than chameleon; both quarrel.
proverbs.usage: When ọgụmagana was born, earth was muddy, so he goes slowly; hornbill said that there was no earth when he was born, and buried his mother in his head. A book-savvy man is older than an ignoramus.

proverbs.igbo: A sị nwata gakpọta nna ya ka o rie ihe; o sị na agụ na-agụ ya, ọ gaghị eje.
proverbs.english: They say to a child, go and call father to eat; he says he is too hungry to go.
proverbs.usage: A man who sits at home does not know what they do at the meeting.

proverbs.igbo: Nwanna dị onye k'okwe j'ụbe anwa mw'ọda.
proverbs.english: A kinsman is one who takes a stick to pick an ube (plum) and finds it when it falls.
proverbs.usage: A witness must be conversant with the case.

proverbs.igbo: Onye dị ụra adịghị eje akaebe.
proverbs.english: One who sleeps does not go as witness.
proverbs.usage: Those who have not been to see don't know.

proverbs.igbo: Ihe onye ma ka egwu n'ahịa; ihe onye na-amaghị, ọ na-ajụ ya n'ahịa.
proverbs.english: Not to know.

proverbs.igbo: Anya onye hụrụ, ọ gaa obi.
proverbs.english: A man's eyes are witness; he goes to obi.
proverbs.usage: No one knows without being told.

proverbs.igbo: Ụbọchị onye ma ihe niile ka ọ nwụọ.
proverbs.english: The day one knows all, let him die.
proverbs.usage: One can always learn.

proverbs.igbo: Ngwere nwa sị, 'Ọsọ ụtụtụ bụ ọsọ.'
proverbs.english: The lizard said, running in the morning is running.
proverbs.usage: It is hard to learn late in life.

proverbs.igbo: Anyị na ị mabe nkakwụ na ijiji; ijiji anwụ akwa, abụba agụ akwụ arụ.
proverbs.english: We and you will not do as flies and yamstick; the stick holds insects' wings, the wings drop off.
proverbs.usage: You can't kill a man because he does not know.

proverbs.igbo: Bịa ka m gwa gị ihe na-akụ nti ọkọ.
proverbs.english: Come and I'll tell you something that tickles the ear.
proverbs.usage: One that does not begin cannot finish.

proverbs.igbo: Ọgụ kwarụ, ọrụ abụrụ.
proverbs.english: If the hoe handle breaks, the work is spoilt.
proverbs.usage: When a promise cannot be carried out on account of sickness.

proverbs.igbo: Ụbè ruru enyi ka e ji atọ.
proverbs.english: It is the spear that suits the elephant that they take to spear it; a gift must be suitable.

proverbs.igbo: A dịghị eji okwu abụọ afịa nwaanyị, ekwe na-abụ.
proverbs.english: People don't flatter a woman twice and have connection.
proverbs.usage: When a man persuades a boy by promises not carried out.

proverbs.igbo: Okenye takịta, ha tụ afịa.
proverbs.english: Traders tell many tales, they give them money (wares) to sell or exchange.
proverbs.usage: If a man gives a trader money in consideration of promises and loses by it.

proverbs.igbo: Okpanam si na ha asụ ebune, na ha eri atụrụ.
proverbs.english: Okpanam says they forbid ram and eat sheep.
proverbs.usage: Of a man who takes gifts from an enemy.

proverbs.igbo: Ije dim unu adịghị eli ọgọ.
proverbs.english: "I am in a hurry" does not get a present.
proverbs.usage: Extravagance.

proverbs.igbo: Ala na-amị ji anaghị eto ọhịa
proverbs.english: A land that bears many yams never grows a bush.
proverbs.usage: Reckless kindness keeps a man poor.

proverbs.igbo: Ihe na-atọ ụtọ na-egbu
proverbs.english: What is sweet kills.
proverbs.usage: To one who goes to excess.

proverbs.igbo: Ọka nwa ọ dara tụọ ọkankị, ka ọ gaa mgba, eteme ka ọ nọkwa na-agba
proverbs.english: Oka makes a 'low collar' that he may stop wrestling, but he still wrestles.
proverbs.usage: Said of a man given a task beyond him.

proverbs.igbo: Ọrịa ka ike; onye na-ebu ọrịa, ọ dịghị mma
proverbs.english: Sickness passes a strong man; no one takes sickness and is good (well).
proverbs.usage: He cannot make a farm.

proverbs.igbo: A sị mmadụ adịghị ike ịlụ ọgụ, ọtụtụ na-abịa ịlụ ya ọgụ
proverbs.english: They say if a man is not strong to fight, many come to fight him.
proverbs.usage: If a man plans and changes his mind.

proverbs.igbo: Onye ụkọ na-aka nzu, ọ ghara ịke oke; ọ bụrụ na o kee oke, mụọ ga-esi n'anya ya pụta
proverbs.english: The priest draws chalk (line); let him not divide property; if he divides property, a spirit will go out from his eye.
proverbs.usage: When a man proposes to fight with one who is stronger.

proverbs.igbo: Ngwere na-arị nkwụ onye nwe ya na-anọghị, ọ gaghị arị n'ihu ya
proverbs.english: The lizard climbs the palm-tree of its owner in his absence; it will not climb before his face.
proverbs.usage: No one can seize the property of a strong man to his face.

proverbs.igbo: Kedị anụ na-atụ mmiri n'ahụ enwe?
proverbs.english: Where is this animal that shakes down water on the monkey?
proverbs.usage: Reply of a big man whose opinion is questioned.

proverbs.igbo: Onye karị onye na-ara ihe o nwere; ọ dị ka onye jide.
proverbs.english: One who surpasses another takes what he has; it is as if he gives him things to hold.

proverbs.igbo: Onye karị onye emeri ya.
proverbs.english: One that surpasses another prevails.

proverbs.igbo: Otu onye ije, ọ tọọ gọọ.
proverbs.english: One goes, it bends.
proverbs.usage: When one is summoned and two come (one as witness).

proverbs.igbo: Akpatakpị sị na ya tinye isi n'ite; ma ọ baraghị ọbara, a maghị ewete ya.
proverbs.english: White-headed lizard says he puts his head in pot; if it is not red, he cannot take it from pot.
proverbs.usage: A strong man must drive his enemy before he returns.

proverbs.igbo: Ọrịa ka dike.
proverbs.english: Sickness surpasses the strong man.

proverbs.igbo: Ife mere onye iwe obi, ọ dị ka ọ wuteghị ya.
proverbs.english: What happens to a brave man does not pain him.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ dịghị adị otu onye jee ahịa na onye nọ n'ụlọ.
proverbs.english: It is not the same thing to go to market and stay at home.
proverbs.usage: Health and sickness are not the same.

proverbs.igbo: Mbe m agwa gị: n'ubu ka a na-ebu akpa.
proverbs.english: Then I will tell you: on the shoulder they rest the bag.
proverbs.usage: When weaker man overcomes.

proverbs.igbo: Mbeku na ibe ya jee egwu; Mbeku si ibe ya, lia afa, nke ya bụ unu niile.
proverbs.english: The tortoise and his fellows go to a dance; the tortoise says to his fellows to get dance names, his own being 'you all'; one cannot eat food cooked by all, and all can eat food cooked by one.

proverbs.igbo: Onye nọdụrụ sị na be ya, ọ ka.
proverbs.english: One sat and said in his house: it is too much.
proverbs.usage: When a man has trouble, he thinks it is the biggest in the world.

proverbs.igbo: Nke afụ onye adịghị afụ ibe ya ka ọ na-afụ n'afọ.
proverbs.english: What one suffers is not the same as what another suffers.
proverbs.usage: When people complain of small troubles.

proverbs.igbo: Amụla m, ọ bụghị m kere onwe m; ọ dị k'okwu ejaka.
proverbs.english: Laugh not at me, because I did not make myself; as it is, the word is left.
proverbs.usage: When a man falls sick and looks ill, and people laugh at him.

proverbs.igbo: Ike nọkọnọ omụọ ọjọọ.
proverbs.english: One who toils becomes workshy.
proverbs.usage: Of a man who meets with misfortune late in life (by younger men who don't know).

proverbs.igbo: Mmiri adịghị aka onye nwe ụlọ amụ ihe.
proverbs.english: Rain is not wiser than the householder.
proverbs.usage: A man can escape trouble.

proverbs.igbo: Ngwere ncha amabasia afọ n'ala, amaghị nke afọ na-ata.
proverbs.english: All lizards lie belly to ground; one does not know whose belly gripes.
proverbs.usage: Each has his own troubles.

proverbs.igbo: Afọ ka ụkẹlẹ dị.
proverbs.english: It is in the belly that cleverness is.
proverbs.usage: If the belly pains, a man keeps quiet.

proverbs.igbo: O si n'isi rịdata n'ubu.
proverbs.english: It came down from the head upon the shoulder.
proverbs.usage: When umunna assists an ill-doer to prevent more misfortune.

proverbs.igbo: Yelele ka ha bịa, velele ka ha kwe; egwu ncha ha tị, anwụ nyelele.
proverbs.english: They sing nothing, they chorus nothing; all their song comes to nothing.
proverbs.usage: When farm turns out badly.

proverbs.igbo: Onye na-ekwe tui tui, ha ziga ya mmụọ.
proverbs.english: Whoever always says 'yes, yes,' they send him to the mmụọ.
proverbs.usage: A man will meet with misfortune if he is weak.

proverbs.igbo: Onye nchụpụ, ọ bụ gị nkịtị, ọ bụ gị azụ kpụ n'ala.
proverbs.english: An exile is wasted and desolate.

proverbs.igbo: Ezi sị okwu, obi gbuo ya.
proverbs.english: If a pig makes palaver, the obi kills it.
proverbs.usage: If two hunters quarrel.

proverbs.igbo: Uchichi abaghị ọgụ.
proverbs.english: Night is never empty of fighting.
proverbs.usage: There will be a fight every night.

proverbs.igbo: Mmadụ ọfega na-akpata esemokwu.
proverbs.english: A forward man provokes strife.

proverbs.igbo: Atụọ ji, mbe amụọ akwụ.
proverbs.english: When they take away yam, poverty comes upon the farm.
proverbs.usage: When friend quarrels after gaining what he wants.

proverbs.igbo: Enyi daa n'oke ala na ala.
proverbs.english: An elephant fell at the boundary of a town and a town.
proverbs.usage: When parties to a palaver are really at one.

proverbs.igbo: Ụkwụ jee eke, ọ yịrị adanu.
proverbs.english: If a foot walks much, he wears adanu (blue bead).
proverbs.usage: When towns have palaver and messengers are seized.

proverbs.igbo: A na-akwụ mmiri, mmiri ọzọ na-abịa.
proverbs.english: Take water out, other water runs in.
proverbs.usage: When one palaver is done another begins.

proverbs.igbo: Adịghị m eji imi achọ ihe na-esi isi.
proverbs.english: I don't take my nose to find what smells.
proverbs.usage: A man with palaver must be able to explain matters to helpers, not ask them to find out.

proverbs.igbo: Ụkwụ buru ọka mma, ọ na-alu.
proverbs.english: A foot carries fine grass.
proverbs.usage: If brother always causes palaver, umunna says this.

proverbs.igbo: Anụ m na nwamba na-arịa ọrịa, ma ahụghị m ya na anya.
proverbs.english: Suddenly I heard that a cat was suffering from syphilis, but have not seen it.
proverbs.usage: When quarrellers ask person to come as witness.

proverbs.igbo: Akpụkpa bụ ihe, kịsa bụ iche.
proverbs.english: Craw-craw troubles one way, small-pox another.

proverbs.igbo: Dike abụọ zute n'ụzọ, ọ dịghị mma.
proverbs.english: Two strong men meet, it is not good.
proverbs.usage: If two want to fight.

proverbs.igbo: Nwata adịghị eri anya anụ.
proverbs.english: A child does not eat the eyes of an animal; a child does not cause war.

proverbs.igbo: Okwu baa n'ego, nwa ogbenye na-aga n'ọsọ.
proverbs.english: A palaver comes to money, the child of a poor man goes aside.
proverbs.usage: If war comes, young men fight; when they make peace old men judge.

proverbs.igbo: Akpụ bụ iyi, oji bụ okoro.
proverbs.english: The cotton tree is a coward, the iroko is a man.
proverbs.usage: When a fighter dodges a matchet.

proverbs.igbo: Aka nri asi na ya ji ofo, aka ekpe asi na ya ji ofo; ofo amaghị onye fịrị okwu.
proverbs.english: The right hand says it has ofo, the left hand says it has ofo; ofo does not know who spoilt his word.
proverbs.usage: When people will not decide a palaver and leave it to mwọ.

proverbs.igbo: O dara, si ha fee ife o bu.
proverbs.english: He falls and tells people to see what he carries.
proverbs.usage: When friends quarrel and one explains the cause.

proverbs.igbo: Ife siri ike, ọ dịghị akarị glegede.
proverbs.english: However big a thing is, it is not bigger than the biggest.
proverbs.usage: When small and big fight and small wins.

proverbs.igbo: Agha ekweghị na oke na-alụ ọgụ.
proverbs.english: War does not agree that a rat fights.
proverbs.usage: If quarrellers are stopped, they remember when they get home how they should have abused each other.

proverbs.igbo: Ọpi na-ara dike n'ime ụlọ ka ọ zobe.
proverbs.english: The flute takes the strong man into the house and stays there.
proverbs.usage: When one disputant hides the property of the other in his house.

proverbs.igbo: Okwu kwuru okwu n'ụbọchị e gburu mbi.
proverbs.english: Word is spoken the day the mbi (a forest bird with a spotted collar) is killed.
proverbs.usage: People agreed that the first to kill game should be king and hunter; a child killed mbi in a trap and claimed kingship when others killed big game and received the leg. Used when people agree to combine and some try to escape subsequent palaver.

proverbs.igbo: Ese abụghị n'ụzọ nta, ọ dịghị emechi.
proverbs.english: If there is no quarrel in a narrow path, it will not be shut; no fight without a quarrel.

proverbs.igbo: Akọ kwọ ji e bupu onye afọ ime.
proverbs.english: It takes care that they remove one who swells.
proverbs.usage: Of a difficult palaver.

proverbs.igbo: Ji onye gwụ, ọ lere.
proverbs.english: If a man's yams are done, he considers.
proverbs.usage: When a man gets palaver.

proverbs.igbo: Nkwụ adịghị ebu igụ agba ọsọ.
proverbs.english: Palm tree does not take palm leaf and run away.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụ onye njọ, ọ na-akpọ njọ aha, si na ya bụ ọzọ, na ya bụ idibụ.
proverbs.english: When it is bad for one he takes a bad name, saying he is a chimpanzee, he is a male chimpanzee.
proverbs.usage: Of a man who has trouble with his own ebo; they hunt for him.

proverbs.igbo: Oke rie, ụmụaka rie.
proverbs.english: If elders eat, children eat (i.e., it is the same as if children eat).
proverbs.usage: If ebo sends money to stop palaver and young men get none of it.

proverbs.igbo: Ikpe na-anya onye okpe, ọ na-agwa onye iro ya.
proverbs.english: When a palaver is too much for a man, he complains to his enemy.
proverbs.usage: People of Idumu go to a quarrelsome man.

proverbs.igbo: Ha adịghị ebu ụlọ agba ọsọ ma ọ bụghị ọgụ mere ya.
proverbs.english: They do not carry a house and run if war does not cause it.
proverbs.usage: When two ebo quarrel and one is much stronger.

proverbs.igbo: Ogo ahụghị ihe ọ ga-eri; ọ na-ewere amara tinye di ya.
proverbs.english: A woman does not see things to give food; she takes charity and puts it for her husband.
proverbs.usage: When two towns quarrel and wish to make peace.

proverbs.igbo: Agha adịghị mma n'ọkpụ izizi.
proverbs.english: War is not good at cock crow.
proverbs.usage: When towns wish to make peace.

proverbs.igbo: Mmadụ anaghị egbu mmadụ ihe na-emegbughị ya.
proverbs.english: A man does not kill a man who did not offend him.
proverbs.usage: If two towns quarrel. The King of Ishan was asked by a man to kill him: he refused as he had no quarrel; the king put corn on his chest: a fowl ate one and was shot with medicine; the king said the fowl had offended him.

proverbs.igbo: Ka anyị ezi, amaghị onye ezi ekwunyere.
proverbs.english: Let us go to the yard; we do not know for whom the yard speaks.
proverbs.usage: When a quarreller refuses to go out in reply to a challenge to wrestle.

proverbs.igbo: Ọnwụ adịghị mfe anwụ.
proverbs.english: Death is not easy to die.
proverbs.usage: When people separate quarrellers.

proverbs.igbo: Okwu ụwa adịghị eje n'ike.
proverbs.english: The word of the world does not go by strength.
proverbs.usage: To one in fault, when two quarrel and another intervenes.

proverbs.igbo: A dịghị akwụsị okwu.
proverbs.english: All is never said.
proverbs.usage: When quarrel goes on in spite of interveners.

proverbs.igbo: O tọọ bụ ike nwata; chi lọọ jikọ agwa.
proverbs.english: It tires; telling a quarrelsome man he will be tired before they reply to him.

proverbs.igbo: Otu onye siri ala, ala gụsịrị; ala siri otu onye, ọ gụsịghị.
proverbs.english: One cooks for the town, they eat it up; the town cooks for one man, he does not finish it; a man cannot fight the whole town.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ fọrọ ntịntị ka mkpịsị aka ruo imi.
proverbs.english: There remains little for the finger to reach the nose.
proverbs.usage: Of a man who narrowly escapes palaver, or condemnation; it was a narrow shave (of a man escaping ambush).

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụrụ na onye hụrụ onye, ihe ọ na-eme adị mma.
proverbs.english: If one likes a person, the things he does please one.
proverbs.usage: Of one who raises objections because he does not like the proposer.

proverbs.igbo: Iyi ya kọ bụọ, ọ ga-aka gwoa.
proverbs.english: His losses surpass his companion's, that is, surpass his company.
proverbs.usage: If two quarrel, one of whom has lost much, a third may rebuke the other one thus.

proverbs.igbo: Etule kpọọ mgbada, elu Ebudu.
proverbs.english: To track a duiker reaches Ebudu bush.
proverbs.usage: To cut palaver short rather than follow it up is to find a worse matter.

proverbs.igbo: Onye kwara n'oke, ọ dịghị eghe ya rie.
proverbs.english: One who is free from rat never roasts it and eats; only children eat rats, adults cannot.
proverbs.usage: When foolish palaver is brought before men.

proverbs.igbo: Anyị amasị ajọ ụzọ banye n'ọhịa.
proverbs.english: We don't take a bad road to go to the bush.
proverbs.usage: A man avoids palaver if he can.

proverbs.igbo: Ana m agbala okwu, jiri abalị lie nne; echi efuo, ụtụtụ okwu atọọla.
proverbs.english: I run from palaver, yet bury my mother at night; at dawn the matter comes up.
proverbs.usage: When someone is trying to escape palaver and gets it all the same.

proverbs.igbo: Abụzọ sị, ka ya saa ala izu ike; ọ maghị na onye dị n'ala, ọ bụ ọnwụ.
proverbs.english: The cricket says let him go to the earth to rest; he does not know that whoever goes to earth, it is death.
proverbs.usage: When someone tries to escape palaver and gets it all the same.

proverbs.igbo: Amara n'amara zụa ahịa, adịghị esu okwu.
proverbs.english: Acquaintance and acquaintance trade, there is no palaver.
proverbs.usage: When friends quarrel, outsiders say friends must decide.

proverbs.igbo: Egede adịghị ezi ka Ọmadọmwa si kee ya.
proverbs.english: The drum is not as Ọmadọmwa ties it.
proverbs.usage: To cowardly soldiers. These proverbs are 'blown' on an ivory horn.

proverbs.igbo: Onịka Ezechi, egwu atụ m.
proverbs.english: Onịka, son of Ezechi, I fear.
proverbs.usage: Recalling soldiers after losses.

proverbs.igbo: Ọzọ maara ọrụ, na-egbu igwe; ọzọ amaghị ọrụ, ọ ma afụ.
proverbs.english: If a blacksmith understands work, he cuts iron; if he does not, he will gain nothing.
proverbs.usage: Warning to watch.

proverbs.igbo: Ọdịa oke eme nri.
proverbs.english: The disgrace of a rat spoils food.
proverbs.usage: If enemies are prevailing.

proverbs.igbo: Anya gị ene eke, gị ene Ọgụlụgụ.
proverbs.english: Let eyes see rainbow (see oil palm poles); (Eke Ọgụlụgụ = rainbow) see 176.
proverbs.usage: When enemy tries to take away body.

proverbs.igbo: Isama, ọ bụ ọgụ, isi ya apịtị.
proverbs.english: Isama, the fighting place becomes muddy.
proverbs.usage: When an enemy tries to surround them.

proverbs.igbo: Akwụ akọ amụlụ amala.
proverbs.english: Care (kind of food) gently (paddle).
proverbs.usage: Warning to soldiers.

proverbs.igbo: Nwata lọọ ọkwa, ya anọ oji.
proverbs.english: A child picks okwa, let him not pick kola.
proverbs.usage: When people gather to light and say there is nothing to prevent them.

proverbs.igbo: Oke akwọghị aka, ọ na-eri nri.
proverbs.english: The rat does not wash its hands when it eats food.
proverbs.usage: If someone tries to stop men from going to war.

proverbs.igbo: A na-egbu ewu maka ọkụkọ?
proverbs.english: Is a goat killed for a hen?
proverbs.usage: Rather than fail in war, let a man die.

proverbs.igbo: Ụkwa daa ọfụma, ọ dịghị ekwe ekwe.
proverbs.english: The breadfruit falls well, it never shakes.
proverbs.usage: A good decision settles a case.

proverbs.igbo: A naghị ebu nwa dị n'afọ nye di.
proverbs.english: They don't take a child in the womb and give it to a husband.
proverbs.usage: Don't decide an unheard case.

proverbs.igbo: Anụ na-alọghị jiri Oye chọọ akọ.
proverbs.english: What am I doing? (workless man) takes Oye day to find nuts.
proverbs.usage: When one wishes to hurry over a case.

proverbs.igbo: Ozi ekwe, ozi ala.
proverbs.english: Drum judges, drum decides.
proverbs.usage: When a case is decided in the absence of one party.

proverbs.igbo: Okutulie, ife nụ adị m gị, bialu betolefe n'Obwawo, we ko lu a banye lu Jidaka, ife gkuru ka e jidaka.
proverbs.english: Okutulie, things of the world are not finished, comes to Tolefe at Obwawo, ready to go calls to Jidaka, things are said that he may hold that.
proverbs.usage: When a man goes a message, let him take care what he says.

proverbs.igbo: A na-ebupụ okwu, a dị ebupụ onye ekwu.
proverbs.english: They carry away the palaver but not the talker.
proverbs.usage: A man is not punished for threats.

proverbs.igbo: Onye fụ ihe a fụ n'anya, o mee ihe a na-emebeghị.
proverbs.english: When a man sees what he cannot endure, he has done something that they have not seen before, i.e., something wrong.

proverbs.igbo: OkBöko fy eyi gfifie, m'odo; grwe n'ebe qne n'enu z'gdo, ngabu osisi isi adapu, tibue nwa Obu; Obu si na ei amafy.
proverbs.english: (Bird) sees rat in the day, blows trumpet; monkey where he lives in tree answers trumpet, branch falls, kills child of Obu; Obu says dawn will not come; Obu refuses sympathy; fowl asks why; 'look at her, her children are killed,' Obu accepts her sympathy, etc.
proverbs.usage: When a man sees what he never saw before (cannot endure), people say it is nothing new; why does he do something wrong?

proverbs.igbo: Onye aghụghọ nwụrụ, gwa onye aghụghọ lie ya.
proverbs.english: A cunning man dies, they take a cunning man to bury him.
proverbs.usage: A man who does things in secret and is not found out.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ dị m iwe na-egbu nwa agụ.
proverbs.english: "I am troubled" kills the leopard's child.
proverbs.usage: To a man who breaks law.

proverbs.igbo: Ụra gbuo onye; ma uche agbughị ya: uche gbuo onye, ọ na-anwụ.
proverbs.english: Sleep kills one; thought will not kill him; thought kills him, he dies.
proverbs.usage: When a man acts against better thoughts.

proverbs.igbo: Ji ga-amaka mma ruo ọdọ.
proverbs.english: The yam will be good when you get to the end.
proverbs.usage: If a friend embezzles.

proverbs.igbo: Ngwere abwala ụlọ, ọ jekwaghị akwụkwọ.
proverbs.english: Lizard breaks his house because he does not go to cut leaf.
proverbs.usage: Of a guardian who embezzles and neglects.

proverbs.igbo: Ọsọ gwụ onye ogbu n'ọnụ, mbia okolu ọrịrị.
proverbs.english: Excuse finishes in the mouth of a murderer; he is ready to hang.

proverbs.igbo: Ọrịa ka dike; ọ karịa onye, emerie ya.
proverbs.english: Illness is stronger than a strong man; what is stronger than a man conquers him.
proverbs.usage: If a well man oppresses a sick man of his own accord.

proverbs.igbo: Afọ na-enweghị otubo, ivilivi k'ọ bụ.
proverbs.english: Belly that has no navel, is ivilivi.
proverbs.usage: Of a man that has no conscience.

proverbs.igbo: K'ede nka n'enwe nzele, fa adịghị akwụ nkite.
proverbs.english: How about this has time, they don't do it for nothing.
proverbs.usage: Of injury from unexpected quarter.

proverbs.igbo: Oje na-eje, onye na-ene.
proverbs.english: A walker walks, a gazer gazes.
proverbs.usage: If a wrongdoer catches a wrongdoer.

proverbs.igbo: Njọ dị n'onye mere.
proverbs.english: Evil is with the evil doer.

proverbs.igbo: Onye na-akpọbu onye na-enweghị ike na-akpala onye kere ya.
proverbs.english: He who oppresses the weak is a reproach to his maker.

proverbs.igbo: Otu nkpụ lego n'ala eze.
proverbs.english: One cowry stopped him from being a king.
proverbs.usage: If a man does a kindness and then harm.

proverbs.igbo: Iyi adịghị eli mbụbụ ọdị.
proverbs.english: The water does not swallow an unbroken calabash.

proverbs.igbo: Mmadụ bụ ọdị.
proverbs.english: When a man's labour is vain.

proverbs.igbo: Ife ha bụ nkịtị adịghị mma.
proverbs.english: What keeps silence is not good.
proverbs.usage: When a man suffers in silence. Osa sent a hawk to get meat; he caught a young owl, the owl said nothing; he went to get a chicken, the fowl flew crying after the hawk; the owl was carried back to the nest.

proverbs.igbo: Onye ndidi nwere awẹ.
proverbs.english: A patient man has luck.

proverbs.igbo: Ezi azịza nwayọọ na-ewepu iwe.
proverbs.english: A soft answer turns away wrath.

proverbs.igbo: O dila arọọ fụ azị ụwa.
proverbs.english: He who waits patiently sees the back of the world (i.e., lives long).
proverbs.usage: To a quick-tempered man.

proverbs.igbo: Ọsụ ọfịa agwa di ji na afọ na-abịa
proverbs.english: Osu ofia says to the farmer that the year comes round.
proverbs.usage: Of people impatient to make new yams (time is fixed by the head chief).

proverbs.igbo: Aka onye na-ata nkwu na-achụ onye n'ubi
proverbs.english: The hand of the palm-wine maker drives the maker from the plantation.
proverbs.usage: When a suitor cohabits with a girl too soon.

proverbs.igbo: Onye nọrọ n'ọzọ, ọ hụ ọyịa
proverbs.english: One who sits long with the blacksmith sees his friend.
proverbs.usage: If an adulterer sits with friends, eats and drinks, the husband may come and catch him.

proverbs.igbo: Onye gbụ ogene adịghị edo ikè n'otu ebe
proverbs.english: Who beats the ogene never stands in one place.
proverbs.usage: If a woman can't stay in one man's house.

proverbs.igbo: Ọgọli je n'ụlọ abụọ, ọ ma nke kama ya
proverbs.english: A woman goes to two houses (e.g. gets two husbands); she knows which is better.
proverbs.usage: Of a woman that wants to leave her husband.

proverbs.igbo: Nwunye di na-achọ ihe, nwunye di ya sị akpala ya rie, ka ya akpala rie
proverbs.english: Find and eat; let her find and eat.
proverbs.usage: When wife and husband quarrel; 'don't provide for me,' i.e. she finds husband has nothing.

proverbs.igbo: Mụwa dị ndụ, ọkụkọ nwanyị atụpụ nkem
proverbs.english: While I live, a fowl of a woman does not bite mine to death.
proverbs.usage: Of a father who treats the mother badly (e.g. taking away her things to give to another wife).

proverbs.igbo: Mụwa dị ndụ, ọkpa nne m anaghị afụ
proverbs.english: While I live, corn-ball of my mother is not unsold.
proverbs.usage: Of a father who treats boy's mother badly (e.g. taking away her things to give to other wife).

proverbs.igbo: Ọkpọrọ adịghị eri eri di ya akụ
proverbs.english: A woman does not eat food her husband gives her (she may not eat what she cooks for her husband).

proverbs.igbo: Mụ na gị na-alụ ọbwa na ewi
proverbs.english: It is tree and rat that I and you marry as spouse.
proverbs.usage: If a husband spends more on a wife who has not come to him than on the one he has, the marriage is a tree and rat marriage. Obwa seeds scatter far; ewi thinks there will be more near the tree, but is deceived.

proverbs.igbo: Di ji na-enye ala, ọ na-enye ọnụ ya
proverbs.english: The farmer gives to the ground, he gives to his mouth.
proverbs.usage: Of a stingy man who keeps his wives short, when he asks for another wife.

proverbs.igbo: Afọ na-ebu okwu; ọ dị ka iwe adịghị n'afọ
proverbs.english: The stomach conceals the word; it is as if anger is not in the stomach.
proverbs.usage: If a betrothed wife is taken by A from B, and B passes him without assaulting him.

proverbs.igbo: Onye na-asụ asụ kwuo okwu; ọ dị ka ọ na-ete ose gafu di ya
proverbs.english: A useless woman speaks; it is as though she makes pepper soup that will hurt her husband.
proverbs.usage: If an unloved wife interrupts conversation.

proverbs.igbo: Ọsọ ya adịghị aga ogoli
proverbs.english: One who cannot bear trouble does not go to a woman.
proverbs.usage: To one who quarrels with wife.

proverbs.igbo: Ha amaghị afọ ogoli
proverbs.english: They don't know the stomach (ways) of women.
proverbs.usage: If a wife leaves a man who says he knows her ways.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ siri ike; ọnya atọọ
proverbs.english: It is hard; sore spreads.
proverbs.usage: If a man spends all his substance in bidding against another for a wife.

proverbs.igbo: Achọ di na achọ nwunye adịghị ezute n'ụzọ.
proverbs.english: One seeking a husband and one seeking a wife never meet on the road.
proverbs.usage: When a man has money and cannot find a wife; after spending his money he finds a suitable wife.

proverbs.igbo: Bụta bụta eyim okwu, ma ọ bụghị akwa.
proverbs.english: A running man is like a call, not a cry.
proverbs.usage: When a woman mourns her husband.

proverbs.igbo: Akwụkwọ ogede na-eme lama lama; dịka onweghị ndọka.
proverbs.english: Plantain leaf is shining as though it does not tear.
proverbs.usage: To a virgin who refuses a husband and cares for no man.

proverbs.igbo: Anya akpọ nni na-eri nwe ya, n'isi onye nwe ya ka ọ na-aga, ọ dịghị efu.
proverbs.english: Eyes that spoil go to the head of the owner and are not lost.
proverbs.usage: When a wife bears no children; she has other work.

proverbs.igbo: Omi dịghị ebu mmiri, ọ ga-ebu ntọ.
proverbs.english: A well that does not hold water will hold ashes.
proverbs.usage: When a man's wife bears no children, he does not repudiate her.

proverbs.igbo: Azụ nwere mmiri, ma ọ hụghị ncha ọ ga-eji asa ahụ.
proverbs.english: A fish has water but sees no soap to wash with.
proverbs.usage: A farmer may have many yams but no wife.

proverbs.igbo: Akwụ leni buru ọka okwu.
proverbs.english: Rotten nut brings palaver for the corn.
proverbs.usage: A woman brings trouble to a man.

proverbs.igbo: Anyị amaghị ịkpa agụ na ewu; gị bụ onye ọcha, i nwere ike ịkpa agụ na ewu.
proverbs.english: We cannot tie leopard nor goat; you are a white man, you can tie leopard and goat.
proverbs.usage: (a) Only a white man can order obi. (b) Leopard and goat (husband and co-respondent) come to court together, eat together.

proverbs.igbo: Ekwu kwemefu maka ọkwụ m ọkwụ; idụm, amaghị m ebe di m nọ zi.
proverbs.english: I speak it as a word that is said; idumu, I do not know where my husband is.
proverbs.usage: Husband has never cohabited with wife, though he does with others.

proverbs.igbo: Ọkụkọ mma ọma etiwa ite, etiwa obobwa, n'ọ maara ebe ọ na-aga ụra.
proverbs.english: Fowl wilfully breaks pot, and open pot knows where it goes to sleep.
proverbs.usage: When a woman runs from her husband, they will return her.

proverbs.igbo: Di adịghị mma, nwunye adịghị mma.
proverbs.english: A husband is not good, a wife is not good; it is six of one to half a dozen of the other.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ dịghị n'ọnụnụ di ya.
proverbs.english: It is not the same thing to be a lover and to be a husband (perhaps waiting and marrying).

proverbs.igbo: Di na nwunye rụrụ ụlọ debe okwu.
proverbs.english: A husband and wife build a house for palaver.

proverbs.igbo: Nkwụ adịghị aka, pụkwe ike amaghị.
proverbs.english: Palm tree is not ripe, foot (buttocks) does not know.
proverbs.usage: The people of an ebo know when a man comes to marry a girl. Secrets.

proverbs.igbo: Ụmụ welu nye okporo adịghị enwe isi.
proverbs.english: Counsel they take with a woman has no head.
proverbs.usage: When a man betrays a secret.

proverbs.igbo: Oke ọhịa gwa oke ụnụ si na nkpọdo dị n'ọkụ.
proverbs.english: The bush rat tells the house rat that the (fish) basket is over the fire.
proverbs.usage: If a man reveals secrets.

proverbs.igbo: Odibo eze bụ eze
proverbs.english: A king's servant is king.

proverbs.igbo: Nwata bakute eze, ọ lisi
proverbs.english: Child who runs to king has freedom.

proverbs.igbo: Obu ome adịghị ebu onye a ga-eji ọrụ ni
proverbs.english: A witch does not kill one whom they take as slave to bury.
proverbs.usage: Stranger must go to house of obi; obi's child is a big man.

proverbs.igbo: Ajali sị: na ya ga-eje gafee Oba nwanne ya; n'ọ bụọ ya, ọ dị mma; n'ọ hapụ ya, ọ dị mma
proverbs.english: Axe says: he will go to see Oba his brother; if he kills him it is good; if he keeps him it is good.
proverbs.usage: When a chief calls a young man.

proverbs.igbo: Aji mụrụ ụmụ, sị: nke bụ ụmụ ya soro ya si mmiri; nke na-abụghị ụmụ ya si elu
proverbs.english: A crocodile bears children, says her own follow her to the water; those that are not hers go up. (Ngwelanwu (lizard) is said to be child of aji.)

proverbs.igbo: Okwu eze kwudị onye, ọ nụọ nkpụli iyi
proverbs.english: The word of the king meets one, he swallows iyi ball (stone).
proverbs.usage: If the head chief accused a man, the accused admitted his guilt, whether innocent or guilty.

proverbs.igbo: Eze nwe ala
proverbs.english: The head chief has the land.
proverbs.usage: When people excuse themselves from coming to the head chief.

proverbs.igbo: Orimili lị onye, ọ lịe ọgụ aya
proverbs.english: A river drowns one, it drowns his war medicine.
proverbs.usage: To a reckless man who does not care for his chief.

proverbs.igbo: Ewu chọrọ itinye ọnu n'olu, ọ hụghị onye ga-ekee ya.
proverbs.english: A goat wants to put a small calabash on his neck but does not see one to tie it on.
proverbs.usage: No one can refuse to be made obi at no cost to himself.

proverbs.igbo: A dịghị eji ọlọpọ egbochi ụzọ.
proverbs.english: They don't take olopo tree to shut the road.
proverbs.usage: If two men are good friends, and a son commits adultery with the wife of one, it does not cause a quarrel.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụ ọkẹ taa na-abụ ọrịa; ngwere asị: wazinye ego gọọ ezé.
proverbs.english: The bite that a rat bites turns to disease; the lizard says: lend him money to file his teeth.
proverbs.usage: Friends meet at night to talk; then tell a tale that causes laugh.

proverbs.igbo: Onye na-egbu mbada otu a n'afọ ọzọ.
