proverbs.english: When a hunter kills a duiker, he says "another year" (he will kill).
proverbs.usage: A friend takes a friend's things and tells him.

proverbs.igbo: Ewu nọdibe ji, ọ bụrụ rie.
proverbs.english: If a goat sits near yams it takes and eats.
proverbs.usage: Cultivate a friend if you want benefactions.

proverbs.igbo: Onye na-aga egbụ si udene, akala gịnị i ji efe efe? Ọ bụghị gbụ m, ị gaghị eri m.
proverbs.english: One who goes to be killed says to the vulture: why do you fly over me? If qba does not kill me, you can't eat me.
proverbs.usage: If a friend calumniates a son-in-law, a man cannot take away his daughter.

proverbs.igbo: Akpọ m idide, ọlu ịsụsị ga-eri ya.
proverbs.english: If they gather worms, the work of cutting bush will eat them.
proverbs.usage: If friends stay long to talk, the visitor can say this.

proverbs.igbo: Ha hụ ọkụ ọkọchị, ha wawa ubi.
proverbs.english: They see the light of a dry season, they cut the farm.
proverbs.usage: A reply to 807. We will talk again on occasion.

proverbs.igbo: Aka nkpọnkpọ ekweghị nwa ega kpọọ ụzọ
proverbs.english: A short hand does not allow a tortoise to make a path.
proverbs.usage: When a man cannot return a friend's kindness, he is ashamed and loses his friend.

proverbs.igbo: Okwu dị n'ọnụ ka m ji amara ọyị
proverbs.english: A word in the mouth is what I take to know a friend.
proverbs.usage: Said when a friend deceives.

proverbs.igbo: Ngwele sịrị: ka o weli ọdụ n'ọgụ; onye na-abụ ewere ọnụ kwuo
proverbs.english: One lizard says to another: let us fight with tails; let neither take his mouth to speak.
proverbs.usage: When a friend injures a friend, the latter says this.

proverbs.igbo: Onye were madụ tinye n'iwe abụghị ọyị ya
proverbs.english: Whoever takes a man and puts him in trouble is not his friend.

proverbs.igbo: Mbada sị ibe ya: onye nụ muke muke, ya mụkenye ibe ya, na akpụkpọ ibe ya ka e ji akwụ egwu
proverbs.english: Duiker says to his kin: whoever hears "hunter" should tell his fellows, because it is his kin's skin they take to make a drum.
proverbs.usage: Said to a friend who omits to warn [another].

proverbs.igbo: Nwanne ahụgo ụmụ nwanne, ọ ga-edede ụmụ di ya
proverbs.english: When a sister has seen the children of her sister, she embraces her husband's children.
proverbs.usage: A man tells his friend, not his brother, and is killed.

proverbs.igbo: Onye ọrịa enweghị ọyị
proverbs.english: A sick man has no friend.

proverbs.igbo: Ha na-abụ ọyị dị ka isi na anya
proverbs.english: They are friends like head and eyes.
proverbs.usage: The eyes do not see the head; one does not know a friend's secret.

proverbs.igbo: Elibe adakwọ ọnụma.
proverbs.english: When you eat, you are not vexed.
proverbs.usage: When a man refuses help but makes use of a friend.

proverbs.igbo: Onye na-enweghị nwunye ya bụ ogbenye nke ebo ya.
proverbs.english: He who has no wife is the poor man of his ebo.
proverbs.usage: When a man returns home after work.

proverbs.igbo: Nti pụa obodo, ọ nụ okwu.
proverbs.english: Ears go to town and hear a word.
proverbs.usage: The stay-at-home does not know what happens.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ dị iche n'ọnọdụ na ibi.
proverbs.english: Staying in a place and living there are different.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụ n'ụtụtụ; ọ gaghị adị mma; ọ bụ ugboro abụọ echi.
proverbs.english: Let it be in the morning; it will not be good; twice tomorrow.
proverbs.usage: A man changes his mind after asking a friend to come and finish the matter.

proverbs.igbo: Onye nọ n'okwu pụtara ọnụ.
proverbs.english: He who stays long on a message utters a word.
proverbs.usage: To those who come to listen unasked.

proverbs.igbo: Gbadi egwu n'ụlọ, anyị eti ọnụ.
proverbs.english: The drum is in the house; we beat the mouth.
proverbs.usage: If one man speaks when another should speak.

proverbs.igbo: Mbe nwere otu akwa, ọ naghị ewe ya akwa.
proverbs.english: If a tortoise has only one cloth, he does not take it to sew a dress.
proverbs.usage: To a man who begs for a unique thing.

proverbs.igbo: A na-eche ka ngwere nwee ntutu, anaghị ebe di.
proverbs.english: They wait for the lizard to get hair, and do not go to a husband.
proverbs.usage: To get rid of importunate beggar.

proverbs.igbo: A naghị afịa onye kụrụ ntutu.
proverbs.english: They never flatter one who plants hair.
proverbs.usage: To importunate borrower.

proverbs.igbo: A sị onye nzuzu na chi agwụla, ọ na-achọ anyanwụ.
proverbs.english: They say to the fool that the day is done; he looks for the sun.
proverbs.usage: When a man is twice refused and persists.

proverbs.igbo: A naghị asị Obolo, ọ dịghị ka bụ ebo onye.
proverbs.english: They do not say Obolo (town) while it is not one's ebo.
proverbs.usage: To one who interferes with domestic affairs of another.

proverbs.igbo: Ozu ọhụrụ adịghị eme ihe iyi.
proverbs.english: A fresh corpse is not an ugly sight.
proverbs.usage: When corpse's relatives do not attend funeral.

proverbs.igbo: Ozu anaghị anụ isi onwe ya.
proverbs.english: A dead body cannot smell itself.

proverbs.igbo: Ihere adịghị eme ozu.
proverbs.english: A corpse feels no shame.

proverbs.igbo: Agu buru onye, ọ buru onyinyo ya.
proverbs.english: Leopard carries off someone, it carries his shadow; the shadow dies with the man.

proverbs.igbo: Ọnwụ enweghị ebere.
proverbs.english: Death has no pity.

proverbs.igbo: Ọnwụ ka mma karịa ọrịa na-atịta.
proverbs.english: Death is better than long sickness.

proverbs.igbo: Ọnwụ enweghị ọgwụ.
proverbs.english: Death has no medicine.

proverbs.igbo: Ọnwụ ajụghị onye.
proverbs.english: Death refuses no one.

proverbs.igbo: Okwu ụwa enweghị ụzọ abụọ; anyị ga-aga ọzọ fee anyị ike wepụ otu ụzọ.
proverbs.english: The word of the world has no two roads; we should have gone to the blacksmith to sharpen an axe to shut one way.
proverbs.usage: When a mourner thinks of suicide.

proverbs.igbo: Ọchụ anaghị agba ihe ọ na-ahụghị anya.
proverbs.english: The hunter does not shoot what he does not see.
proverbs.usage: A man cannot pay what he did not see.

proverbs.igbo: Mgbe ọ bụ ọgụ, ukwu na aka tere aka.
proverbs.english: When one is ready to wrestle, leg and hand are far.
proverbs.usage: If a man cannot find money to buy what he needs and wants to borrow though he is a notorious debtor.

proverbs.igbo: Chere m ka m tụkọ mmiri, amaghị nke chi mere ya.
proverbs.english: "Wait for me to bathe" does not know what chi has done to him.
proverbs.usage: A man who can wash quickly (i.e., has no sore) does not realise his good fortune.

proverbs.igbo: Ji na-adọ n'ubi, ọ lụọ ọlụ mba.
proverbs.english: Yams stay in the farm and get good seed; one who lives long meets with good fortune.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụ eme ka i daba mba ngelengele.
proverbs.english: When a man uses a bad climbing rope.

proverbs.igbo: Nke na-akpa onye adịghị akpa ibe.
proverbs.english: What troubles one does not trouble another; tastes differ.

proverbs.igbo: A naghị ahọpụtara mmadụ oyi.
proverbs.english: They don't choose a friend for a man; tastes differ.

proverbs.igbo: Ife onye nwe, ibe adịghị enwe; ijiji nwere akwa, ngwere na-aga ọtọ.
proverbs.english: A thing one has, the other has not; a fly has cloth, a lizard goes naked; people think differently.

proverbs.igbo: Ọgụ eju adịghị agba ọbara.
proverbs.english: The combat of snails is bloodless.
proverbs.usage: Used in defiance: you cannot suit me.

proverbs.igbo: Ọkụnkọ bata n'ụlọ ọba, ọ na-ala n'oyi.
proverbs.english: If a woodman goes to the head wife of Oba, he sleeps in the cold.
proverbs.usage: If one man tries to injure another, it is useless.

proverbs.igbo: Akụ jee n'okwute, adịghị enwe nkọ.
proverbs.english: The arrow that hits a stone is not sharp again.
proverbs.usage: A doctor cannot poison a doctor; that is, you cannot harm me.

proverbs.igbo: Enyi anaghị anwụ n'ọhịa, a na-agba ya egbe.
proverbs.english: An elephant does not die in the field where they shoot it.
proverbs.usage: When one threatens another, the latter replies.

proverbs.igbo: Otu onye abụghị ala.
proverbs.english: One man is not a town.
proverbs.usage: When a man disregards public opinion.

proverbs.igbo: Alụsị ọcha e gbunem, gịnị ka alụsị ọjị ga-eme?
proverbs.english: A white alose does not kill me; what will a black alose do?
proverbs.usage: When a man disregards a big alose, he disregards a small one.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụghị dibịa na-asa mbụda na ene.
proverbs.english: It is not a doctor who washes duiker and buck.
proverbs.usage: To a man who threatens to poison one.

proverbs.igbo: Kịkịnta si na nwata na-achọ ihe ọ ga-eji gbuo ya, ọ na-achọ ọnụ ụzọ ebe a ga-eli ya.
proverbs.english: A snake says that if a child seeks something to kill it, he seeks the edge of the street where they will bury him (the child).
proverbs.usage: To a man who threatens to poison one.

proverbs.igbo: Agwọ adịghị eje, ọ na-akwala ala.
proverbs.english: A snake does not go straight away.
proverbs.usage: If someone challenges, 'You cannot easily beat me.'

proverbs.igbo: Onye na-eri ihe o nwere, ihe ọ nweghị ka ọ na-achọ.
proverbs.english: A man who eats what he has desires what he has not.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ dị n'uche onye, ma aka adịghị ezu iji mee.
proverbs.english: It is in one's mind, but hands are not there to do it; if wishes were horses.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ na-eru onye nwere ndidi.
proverbs.english: It reaches one who has patience.
proverbs.usage: When a young man becomes by death the oldest in the idumu.

proverbs.igbo: A naghị ebu mbu weta akalị Izoiya.
proverbs.english: They don't take title earlier than Izoiya (Izoiya got yaws after taking title).
proverbs.usage: To a man aiming at okpala title in youth.

proverbs.igbo: Onye na-akụ obere ji, na-aghọ aghụghọ onwe ya.
proverbs.english: Who plants small seed yam, deceives himself.
proverbs.usage: Give up designs that are too big.

proverbs.igbo: Ọbụ ibu adịghị ebu ani.
proverbs.english: A carrier cannot carry the earth.
proverbs.usage: To one who tries impossibilities.

proverbs.igbo: Oti ukwu adịghị eti ani.
proverbs.english: A fighter cannot fight the earth.
proverbs.usage: To one who tries impossibilities.

proverbs.igbo: Agadi rie, okwele ọgụ.
proverbs.english: An old man eats, he agrees to fight.
proverbs.usage: A man is induced to risk his life when he has something to gain.

proverbs.igbo: Mbeku adịghị arị ukpo.
proverbs.english: A tortoise cannot climb a throne (ukpo).
proverbs.usage: When a man tries something beyond him.

proverbs.igbo: Anyị ahụgo nnụ mmadụ, anyị adịghị akpọzi ọgọ mmadụ ihe.
proverbs.english: We see four hundred men, we do not call two hundred men anything.
proverbs.usage: One does not go out to see a smaller thing than one has already seen.

proverbs.igbo: Mbụ m onye; ọdị abụọ m mara ihe.
proverbs.english: First (thing) does one; the second (time) he knows it.
proverbs.usage: A man learns by experience.

proverbs.igbo: Onye jere aka, ọ hụrụ aka.
proverbs.english: Who walks far, sees much.

proverbs.igbo: Ibebune nwa Nwọmọ sị n'etukwa ani kụọ ọkpụ, na-ele onwe ya anya; ọ ka mma karịa onye kwụ ọtọ.
proverbs.english: Ibebune, son of Nwomo, says that who stoops and beats drum observes himself; he beats better than one who stands.
proverbs.usage: People observe what their fellows do.

proverbs.igbo: Ụwa nke a anyị bịara, ha adịghị eji enwe lie adaka.
proverbs.english: This world we come to, they never take enwe to bury adaka.
proverbs.usage: When monolinguals of different tongues meet, they don't kill each other.

proverbs.igbo: Ọfịa asị akpa ya epụne elo.
proverbs.english: If a bush forbids bag, it must not grow fungus.
proverbs.usage: One who does not wish to be abused, does not abuse. (Do as you would be done by.)

proverbs.igbo: Ndị anya mkpị abụọ zutere n'ụzọ, otu anya aka ekpe, otu anya aka nri.
proverbs.english: Two half blind men meet by the way, one no left eye, one no right eye.
proverbs.usage: Don't ask others to do what you won't do yourself.

proverbs.igbo: Aka nri kwọ aka ekpe; aka ekpe akwọ aka nri.
proverbs.english: The right hand washes the left and the left washes the right.
proverbs.usage: Of mutual respect.

proverbs.igbo: Ajụ abụọ eji ebu aga, eji ebu ọmụnwa; ọmụnwa adịghị aga n'ajụ.
proverbs.english: Two head pads carry sterile woman, they carry a fruitful woman; fruitful woman does not pass sterile with pad.
proverbs.usage: When fruitful woman boasts to sterile woman, two men carry her when she dies, whether she has children or not.

proverbs.igbo: Anị naa amazu, k'ego aka mwa ha abụghị imalegwe.
proverbs.english: The whole country does not meet and tie cowries while they are not imalegwe.
proverbs.usage: When two meet and quarrel, one boasts of his cowry wristlet.

proverbs.igbo: Ọkọkọ sị kpọmpana, ọ bụrụ na ọ na-aga ilo ya, ya loo ya ozugbo, ya na-eme ya amụma ọjọọ, ajụ nye ya n'anya.
proverbs.english: Fowl says to butterfly, if he is going to swallow him, swallow him at once, let him not wilfully make him giddy.
proverbs.usage: No answer to repeated threats.

proverbs.igbo: Oke bwagoro je n'elu nkwụ, ọ sị ozi ziri enyi; ya na-akwụ okpete n'anya, ga-eje akwụ ọmụ.
proverbs.english: The rat runs up oil palms, says he sends messenger to elephant, let him root out sugar cane, that he goes to root out young palm leaves.

proverbs.igbo: Otu mkpụrụ akọ adịghị efu n'ọkụ.
proverbs.english: One nut is not lost in the fire.
proverbs.usage: Of a boaster.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ dịghị ije mmụọ.
proverbs.english: You cannot walk to the other world.
proverbs.usage: To a boaster.

proverbs.igbo: Ka onye kwụ ka ọdị ya; ka adakada jila nwunye ngwere kwụ ụkpọ ego.
proverbs.english: Let one pay according to one's size; dung beetle cohabits with lizard's wife and pays one cowry fine.
proverbs.usage: To a boaster.

proverbs.igbo: Ọkwa egwu adịghị emeri ngwesi.
proverbs.english: A dancer does not dance better than ngwesi (yellow wagtail).
proverbs.usage: To a boaster.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ dịghị iwe dịka onye anwụrụ anwụ.
proverbs.english: They do not feel cross more than one who has smoke in his face.
proverbs.usage: Two rich men boasting.

proverbs.igbo: Ọtọntọ adaghị ọkọ isi.
proverbs.english: A trickster cannot trick the barber.
proverbs.usage: To a boastful trickster.

proverbs.igbo: Akpata sị na ya na-ekwu okwu na nnụ na mwa, onye nwe ya amaghị.
proverbs.english: The guitar says that it speaks 20 and 400, but its owner does not know.
proverbs.usage: Used in a quarrel when a young man boasts of his progress.

proverbs.igbo: Onye amala adịghị apị n'apịtị.
proverbs.english: The paddler does not paddle in the mud.
proverbs.usage: Of one who talks of himself against another; one leg does not stand up. If two men begin a title and only one finishes and boasts, the other replies, 'You had backers.'

proverbs.igbo: Nnụnụ adịghị efe nke ọbụna, nwa Ako.
proverbs.english: A bird does not fly like an egret, child of Ako.
proverbs.usage: To a boaster: he cannot be richer than the king.

proverbs.igbo: Otu onye adịghị eguzo n'ụzọ abụọ.
proverbs.english: One man does not stand in two roads.
proverbs.usage: To a man who boasts of many children (it takes a woman also).

proverbs.igbo: Osisi ọ dịghị ka onwala mma.
proverbs.english: No tree is finer than onwala.
proverbs.usage: To a boaster who has no wife or child.

proverbs.igbo: Anyanwụ ụtụtụ akaghị akwa; nke anyasị bụ abwọlọ.
proverbs.english: The morning sun does not dry clothes; the evening sun is weak (not strong enough to dry).
proverbs.usage: When a man who has not worked at all boasts of when he will finish.

proverbs.igbo: Agụ bụ onye ọma, gbazụ bụ onye ọma, agụ gbuo gbazụ bụ gbazụ nkịli.
proverbs.english: The leopard is a good creature, and the guinea fowl is too; the leopard kills the guinea fowl and keeps looking at it.
proverbs.usage: When rivals try to eclipse each other and spoil each other's show.

proverbs.igbo: Onye Agolo sị eyi: ebwana gbaa, ọ bụ mụ na gị n'ala Agolo; ebwana gbaga, ọ bụ mụ na gị n'ala Agolo.
proverbs.english: If you do not run, it is you and me in Agolo.
proverbs.usage: If two boasters meet, 'wait till year comes.'

proverbs.igbo: Nkịta amaghị eteta ụla, zịzịpụ ntụ; ebe ọ maghị ute, anyasị alaghachikwa na ntụ.
proverbs.english: The dog does not wake in the morning and shake off the ashes; but if it does not order a mat, in the evening it sleeps in the ashes again.
proverbs.usage: Of idle boasting of a man who has done nothing.

proverbs.igbo: Onye n'uche, onye n'uche.
proverbs.english: Who has his opinion, has his opinion.
proverbs.usage: To obstinate man.

proverbs.igbo: Mba, e wem aka, ndụ pịa onye aka.
proverbs.english: I cannot crush my hand because of insects.
proverbs.usage: Refusal.

proverbs.igbo: K'ị ma aka ihe, ị ma gọ ijiji ụnyaahụ?
proverbs.english: As you know a thing, did you know the fly of yesterday?
proverbs.usage: Used especially by women; if a woman refuses, e.g., salt to one from whom she borrows often.

proverbs.igbo: Ọgọli mụaka, ọ danyeghị onwe.
proverbs.english: A woman is fine, she does not marry herself.
proverbs.usage: Girl who refuses suitors.

proverbs.igbo: Ọchụta amụghị mgbada, atawo aka; n'ụtụtụ echi ọ ga-ahụ ya.
proverbs.english: A hunter misses a duiker, bites his finger; at dawn next day he will see it.
proverbs.usage: When a man's request is refused.

proverbs.igbo: Ọsa sị enunokwu zịdete, sị plili gaa kpanye ekwele.
proverbs.english: Squirrel comes down from palm and says to ground squirrel: go and get me cord (from tree).
proverbs.usage: Refusal to do what is requested.

proverbs.igbo: Anụ m na-afa na-eyi aja otu obwe, ma nke obwe na-abọ amaghị m.
proverbs.english: I hear they make sacrifice for bad travelling, but for coming back I don't know.
proverbs.usage: One thing at a time (?); refusal to fall in with a suggestion.

proverbs.igbo: Efi sị na ọ masị ya iso ndị ahịa ije; ọ daa, ndị ahịa agaghị ebu ya.
proverbs.english: The cow says it pleases her to walk with traders; if she falls the traders will not carry her.
proverbs.usage: Refusal to accompany messenger.

proverbs.igbo: A dajụ onye ka ọ sị kọ ntọ ya.
proverbs.english: They don't ask one how he scratches his sore.
proverbs.usage: A man who refuses to cease at bidding.

proverbs.igbo: Owu dị n'isi ka oke jiri aha ọmangana.
proverbs.english: Fame is on the head as the rat takes the name of omangana (one who sits in one place).
proverbs.usage: If a lame man, e.g., is successful.

proverbs.igbo: Ọgọli dị n'udo n'ihi na ọ bụ naanị ya n'ụlọ di ya.
proverbs.english: A woman is quiet because she alone is in husband's house.
proverbs.usage: People interfere only with successful man.

proverbs.igbo: Nkịtị ọsa gbụrụ akwụ, ọsa a sara ike pịju ọdọdọ.
proverbs.english: Ever since the squirrel cut nuts it has never been able to fill calabash with oil.
proverbs.usage: Of an unsuccessful man who works hard.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ dị mma inye enwe mmanya, ma onye ga-eweta ọkwa?
proverbs.english: It is fitting to give palm wine to a monkey; but who will bring the calabash back?
proverbs.usage: When a farmer sees he succeeds less than a man who planted less.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ na-eme m n'amaghị m; ma m maara, gịnị ka m ga-eme?
proverbs.english: He troubles me because I did not know; if I had known what should I have done?
proverbs.usage: Unsuccessful man tries various plans.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ dịghị ịkọbi esi ọkwa ma mmiri ngọ adịghị na ya.
proverbs.english: One can try hard for riches, but fail if it is not his lot.

proverbs.igbo: Mmiri ọbụwa ji awọ ahụ, ka ugo ji ncha ịsa ahụ; nke ugo abara ugo n'ife.
proverbs.english: One's labour is useless, another's fruitful.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ tẹ anya bịa n'isi.
proverbs.english: It is long when the eye comes to the head.
proverbs.usage: Of long and fruitless discussion; postponement.

proverbs.igbo: Hapụ ebwe, kwebe n'ebe ọ kwụtị.
proverbs.english: Leave ebwe (tree), let it stand where it stands.
proverbs.usage: Postponing action (if one is in trouble).

proverbs.igbo: Ụzọ dị owu, nduru eburu akpa.
proverbs.english: Road is cool, dove takes up bag.
proverbs.usage: To an unwelcome or inconvenient visitor; 'come another time,' when a man has other business and postpones a caller.

proverbs.igbo: Ụsụ si nne n'ime afọ, ọ ga-amụ ya, ya amụnye n'afọ.
proverbs.english: Bat tells mother while in womb, if she delays to deliver her, she will bear her own child in womb.
proverbs.usage: To procrastinator.

proverbs.igbo: Ọnwụ dịkebe nwa ọkete, ọ ga-eto ka nne nkwụ.
proverbs.english: Children will grow up.

proverbs.igbo: Okenye tosie, ọ cịa ibe.
proverbs.english: A child may be ill-treated but not a man.

proverbs.igbo: Lege lege bụ m udụ; mkpịsị aka nwata adabaghị n'anya eje.
proverbs.english: A child talks nonsense: a child's finger does not go through the eye of a bead.
proverbs.usage: A child cannot abuse a grown person.

proverbs.igbo: Nwata adịghị egwu Nkpetime.
proverbs.english: A child does not swim Nkpetime (pond).
proverbs.usage: A child must pay attention.

proverbs.igbo: Okwu bụ ọkpọlọ, ebe a tụlonye ya, mbia osi.
proverbs.english: A word is hard clay; where they throw it, it goes.
proverbs.usage: A child and a big man do not know the same things.

proverbs.igbo: Nwata gara njem maara ihe karịa oke nọ n'ụlọ.
proverbs.english: A travelled child knows better than the old man who sits at home.
proverbs.usage: If a young man's advice is refused, when he has learnt from his father.

proverbs.igbo: Onye na-anụghị ihe, ọnwụ bụ enyi ya.
proverbs.english: One who cannot hear, death is his companion.
proverbs.usage: When young men refuse the advice of an older man.

proverbs.igbo: Ịhụ ngkụ na-egbu oke; ekwu na-anụ na-egbu ikolo.
proverbs.english: Seeing and keeping silence kills an old man; speaking and hearing kills the young men.
proverbs.usage: When young men refuse the advice of an older man.

proverbs.igbo: Ọgọdọ abụghị enyi iyi.
proverbs.english: A pond is not a companion of a river.
proverbs.usage: If a young man tries to join his elders.

proverbs.igbo: Ọlịlị bọọ ọka, ọ na-ezo.
proverbs.english: If ground squirrel digs up corn, he hides.
proverbs.usage: When a young man acts in defiance of others.

proverbs.igbo: Azị na-aṅụrị ọṅụ n'ụtụtọ; onweghị onye na-agba afa ihe ụwa ga-abụ n'anyasị.
proverbs.english: The present generation rejoices in the morning; no one divines what the world will be in the evening.
proverbs.usage: To careless young men.

proverbs.igbo: Abụ m kwụ n'ụzọ na-akwadebe n'anyasị ụmụma dị n'ihu m.
proverbs.english: One who has to start early prepares in the evening against dawn.
proverbs.usage: A young man must not lose his opportunity.

proverbs.igbo: Onye dị onye ka mara ihe.
proverbs.english: One who is older than another knows more.
proverbs.usage: To forward young men.

proverbs.igbo: Ọkọrọ zọọ ụzọ akasị; ọ bụ enyi n'ọnọli.
proverbs.english: Woman plants koko too early; she plants over spare ground (that her husband does not plant).
proverbs.usage: Rebuke to a young man who tries to explain the case to the whole town instead of leaving it to the chief to do.

proverbs.igbo: Nwata adaghị ije izizi akpọfe mmiri.
proverbs.english: A child does not begin to walk and jump over a well.
proverbs.usage: If young men speak without knowledge.

proverbs.igbo: Nwata kwọọ aka, o soro ọgaranya rie nri.
proverbs.english: A boy washes his hands and follows a rich man to eat.
proverbs.usage: When a young man offers his opinion and it is approved by older men.

proverbs.igbo: Ofili onye Oniọma, si ndị jekọ iyi zido ibu n'ala, ka ya bụ ala a na-agaghị aga.
proverbs.english: Ofili of Oniomma tells those that go take inyi: put down loads on ground, that he is a country they never pass over.
proverbs.usage: When the young men try to decide what old men should deal with.

proverbs.igbo: Agadi ka aka, ewebea nri.
proverbs.english: When an old man gets too old, they give him less food.
proverbs.usage: An old man cannot work like a young one.

proverbs.igbo: Iwe na nwa obu yi ọkọ, ebo adịghị eyi
proverbs.english: Anger makes the child of obu wear oko cloth his ebo does not wear.
proverbs.usage: If young men refuse and elders have to do work forbidden to them.

proverbs.igbo: Nwata bụ ọga, ọ bụrụ ọkụkọ; ọ bụrụ ewu, a họrọ oke nwoke
proverbs.english: A child is a divider if it is a fowl; if it is a goat, they choose a grown man.
proverbs.usage: When old men send young men to work, they don't send for them to share money.

proverbs.igbo: Adịghị ebe a na-egbu ene
proverbs.english: They do not take a hunter's killing of a bush buck.
proverbs.usage: If a new hand overthrows an old wrestler.

proverbs.igbo: Okeleku adịghị akpa n'ụlọ okokporo
proverbs.english: A lad does not collect in a bachelor's house.

proverbs.igbo: Iche iche ka ihe nni si agwụ
proverbs.english: In different ways food utensils perish.
proverbs.usage: Young and old are different.

proverbs.igbo: Ụdene tọọ ihe ọnụ, e were gbaba nye ya
proverbs.english: A vulture touches a thing with his mouth; they cut and give him.
proverbs.usage: If an older man comes to a palm wine drinker, he gets a big share.

proverbs.igbo: Mma jee ubi ropụta ji ise; ọ bụrụ na njọ jee, ncha ji dị ubi agwụ
proverbs.english: Good went to the farm and dug five yams; if bad went, all the yams would have been finished.
proverbs.usage: If young men all asked to speak in a meeting.

proverbs.igbo: Ọdịda amaghị oke
proverbs.english: Falling does not know an old man.

proverbs.igbo: Ka anya onye dị, ka ọ na-ahụ ụzọ.
proverbs.english: As one's eyes are, so he sees the road.
proverbs.usage: Young man should not raise laugh at meeting.

proverbs.igbo: Maka mmiri na-ama Azọma, nwunye Ọba, oke nwoke na nwanyị isi ọba ga-ebinye.
proverbs.english: Because the rain beats Azoma, wife of Oba, men's and women's heads Oba will cut off.
proverbs.usage: There are old people in every town. Oba (the King of Benin) was young when his father died; all the wives but Azoma were carried off. The doctor told Oba to sacrifice her at the end of the street, to boil two hundred headpads and put them before the door, and to go to the ukbo and lie on his belly lamenting. At dawn Iyase came and asked why he lamented; he said the two hundred pads were for loads brought by Ezomo to hand over as his father's property. Iyase begged for forgiveness and all the property was returned. At the end of the year he built a house where Azoma was sacrificed, and men and women sacrificed annually. This story I found in a very similar form in Benin City.

proverbs.igbo: Ife adịghị edo ọka, ọ na-edo obodi.
proverbs.english: The fool doubts what the wise man does not doubt.
proverbs.usage: Old men are good counsellors.

proverbs.igbo: Agụ na-ebutere isi nkọ.
proverbs.english: Old age brings baldness.
proverbs.usage: To one who laughs at bald men.

proverbs.igbo: A naghị ebu ji egosi onye gwuru ya.
proverbs.english: Yams are not taken to show the one who dug them.
proverbs.usage: An outsider cannot explain to the owner what he has.

proverbs.igbo: Onye nwe ala ka ike.
proverbs.english: One who rules the town is stronger.
proverbs.usage: Strangers must lose the day.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ biakwa ka ọbịa bụ ohi nwa dị n'ala; afụ nene afụ nene bụ ohi otu mmiri.
proverbs.english: The old thief comes as he came before; it is the first time when it's a strange thief.
proverbs.usage: A stranger introduces a habit of theft.

proverbs.igbo: Ọdịda adịghị ewufu ihe dị n'afọ; onye dara ebulu nke ya, bilie.
proverbs.english: Falling does not throw away things in stomach; who falls takes up his and stands up.
proverbs.usage: Strangers don't understand each other as friends do.

proverbs.igbo: Ejebe m ka m pụta, mee ka ha debe nye ife ọ ga-eli.
proverbs.english: "I go and am coming back" makes people keep things for him to eat.

proverbs.igbo: Aka dọọ igili, ka igili so.
proverbs.english: Hand draws "bush rope," let igili follow.
proverbs.usage: A man must come in reply to a message.

proverbs.igbo: Ngwa ngwa ka ha na-ala onye ekpenta.
proverbs.english: Quickly they copulate a leper.
proverbs.usage: By messenger, to hurry one he calls.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụghị sọ n'ọmụmụ ka nkịta na-aza okwu, ọ na-azazikwa nke na-amụghị nwa.
proverbs.english: It is not only a fruitful woman that a dog answers; he answers one who is sterile.
proverbs.usage: If a small man calls a meeting, or for help.

proverbs.igbo: Agụnkwo nwụrụ, ihe gburu ọkụkọ adịghị agwụ.
proverbs.english: If the kite is dead, what kills fowl is not finished.

proverbs.igbo: Akwa dịkwa ebe Nesi kwere ya.
proverbs.english: Cloth is where Nesi fixed it.
proverbs.usage: If a man who calls a meeting is not ready to deal with the matter.

proverbs.igbo: A na-ebu uzo, ọ nweghị mbana.
proverbs.english: They never make a farm without a road.
proverbs.usage: When no one replies in a meeting.

proverbs.igbo: Akpịkpọ folo adịghị ezi ozi.
proverbs.english: A featherless arrow does not fly.
proverbs.usage: A drunkard does not prosper.

proverbs.igbo: Mmanya bara, ọzọ abịa.
proverbs.english: Palm wine enters, noise comes.
proverbs.usage: Names.

proverbs.igbo: Ene da
proverbs.english: Look to the end.
proverbs.usage: To one who talks without knowledge.

proverbs.igbo: Ụwa ra iwe.
proverbs.english: Let the world leave off anger.
proverbs.usage: When a poor man gets rich and his companions murmur.

proverbs.igbo: Asịa erue mụọ.
proverbs.english: (Term of abuse) reaches the spirit.
proverbs.usage: Sterile woman who bears a child after being abused and laughed at for sterility can name her child thus.

proverbs.igbo: Anyị nọkwa ebe anyị nọ; anyị nọkwa ebe anyị na-eche gị.
proverbs.english: We stay where we stay; we stay to wait for you.
proverbs.usage: When a host says he has no more palm wine, his guests refuse to go and say this.

proverbs.igbo: Nwa nduru nwere ala; onye ntị nkụ asị, unu n'imara.
proverbs.english: Child of dove has land; deaf man says, you know.
proverbs.usage: At Ekwensu dance to people from other towns that they must give way.

proverbs.igbo: Tụm bụ dozie.
proverbs.english: Throw at me is an open place.
proverbs.usage: When a man speaks in parables.

proverbs.igbo: Otu osisi dị n'ihu oba; ọ bọsị ọlụ akwụkwọ kọpụ.
proverbs.english: One tree is in the yard of oba; the day it puts out leaves, they fall off.

proverbs.igbo: Nịndọ na-akpụlụ ndọ akwụ
proverbs.english: The pigeon builds for 'ndo' (green pigeon) a nest.
proverbs.usage: The Creator provides for his creatures.

proverbs.igbo: Kpọn kpọbụ kpọn kpọbụ kpọn kpọbụ amụ
proverbs.english: Children's sign that a strange child is coming: 'Let us go and beat him.'

proverbs.igbo: Okwu adaghị n'ọnụ
proverbs.english: Word never finishes in mouth.
proverbs.usage: There must always be subjects for discussion.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ dịghị ụbọchị ire azaghị ezi
proverbs.english: The day will not dawn that the tongue stops sweeping his yard.
proverbs.usage: We eat every day.

proverbs.igbo: Ozu nwụrụ ọnwụ, ọ dịghị ebu onwe ya
proverbs.english: Corpse dies death, it does not carry itself.
proverbs.usage: A man must do his duty.

proverbs.igbo: Ndị na-ete ọkụrọ agwụsị; ndị fọdụrụ na-eti efere kpankpam
proverbs.english: Those who cook okro soup have done; there remain those who only beat the (empty) plate.
proverbs.usage: Those who know proverbs are dead; we don't know many.

proverbs.igbo: Eri nni, ahụ nkpụrụ ya
proverbs.english: When they eat, they see the seed of it.
proverbs.usage: A word comes, the answer follows.

proverbs.igbo: Ọzọ maara onye ọ na-eji ọtụtụ ekele
proverbs.english: Blacksmith knows whom he salutes with his hammer.

proverbs.igbo: Ahịhịa na-awụ, ahịhịa na-epu.
proverbs.english: The grass dies, the grass springs up.

proverbs.igbo: O nọ n'ala adaghị ada onye n'elu.
proverbs.english: Who is on the ground cannot fall on one who is above.

proverbs.igbo: Otu mkpụrụ na-abụ ọja mmanụ.
proverbs.english: One nut makes much oil; that is, there is only one moon.

proverbs.igbo: Ọkà nụka adịghị anụ olu nne n'ahịa.
proverbs.english: One who hears well cannot hear his mother's voice in the market.

proverbs.igbo: Olu nwe ọla; ọla nwe olu.
proverbs.english: Olu has ọla; ọla has Olu (i.e., one is not a bigger man than the other).

proverbs.igbo: Ka ọ dị na be nwoke, ka ọ dị na be nwaanyị.
proverbs.english: As it is in the abode of man, so it is in the abode of woman.

proverbs.igbo: N'ime ime okwu adịghị njehie.
proverbs.english: In many words there is no mistake.

proverbs.igbo: Mbibi adịghị ike.
proverbs.english: Spoiling is not hard.

proverbs.igbo: Ndụ bụ nnu.
proverbs.english: Life is salt.

proverbs.igbo: Ụbọlọ adịghị egbu awọ.
proverbs.english: Quarter-staff does not kill a frog.
proverbs.usage: No one is killed in friendly quarter-staff play.

proverbs.igbo: Odogu adịghị aba n'ọgba aka efu.
proverbs.english: Odogu can't go to a disturbance and do nothing.

proverbs.igbo: A dọpụ ndị ichie n'ala, atọ mọnya.
proverbs.english: Nothing can be done without the knowledge of the Ike Ani.

proverbs.igbo: Ọkụkọ adịghị aṅụ mmiri echezọ igwe.
proverbs.english: Fowl does not drink water and forget the sky.
proverbs.usage: They remember what white man says.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ dịghị ndị ani akarị efi.
proverbs.english: They are never sons of the soil more than a cow; a white man is wiser than a black (Oyibo bụ mụọ).

proverbs.igbo: Anyị amaghị ike ịgbụ agụ na ewu; ọ bụ onye ọcha nwere ike ịgbụ agụ na ewu.
proverbs.english: We cannot tie leopard nor goat; you are a white man, you can tie leopard and goat.
proverbs.usage: Only a white man can order obi.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ dịghị ihe karịrị ndị ọcha.
proverbs.english: There is nothing bigger than white men.

proverbs.igbo: Enu dị ebe ọ dị, ani dị ebe ọ dị.
proverbs.english: The world is where it is, the earth (land) is where it is.
proverbs.usage: You can make changes but it comes to nothing.

proverbs.igbo: Ndụ abụghị apani.
proverbs.english: Life is not bush rope.
proverbs.usage: If life were visible, enemy would take it away.

proverbs.igbo: Ohi ezuru ya ọnụ.
proverbs.english: A thief steals his mouth.
proverbs.usage: When a man cannot answer.

proverbs.igbo: Mbada nwa Ilota si na ya nwụrụ, na ọ bụ ya na ụdụdụ so nwe.
proverbs.english: Duiker, son of Ilota, says if he is dead it is he and tsetse who have palaver.
proverbs.usage: A hunter kills duiker driven out by tsetse, makes fly whisk of duiker skin.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ bụghị okwu mmadụ.
proverbs.english: It is not the palaver of man (no one's fault).
proverbs.usage: When a man cannot repair mischief.

proverbs.igbo: Ụlọ ete ka a na-esi eje ụlọ nkwụ.
proverbs.english: (It is) the house of the climbing rope that they pass to go to the house of the palm tree.
proverbs.usage: Of go-between.

proverbs.igbo: Ha adịghị elo nto atọ.
proverbs.english: They never plan deceit.
proverbs.usage: 'Judges' say this to helpers of man who fight shy or rat.

proverbs.igbo: Kalama n'isi, kalama n'ibolo.
proverbs.english: Cunning man you do not take, cunning man you do not bury.
proverbs.usage: If man raises a laugh instead of talking seriously.

proverbs.igbo: Ebe ha nọ bụ Ebune iyi, ka ha na-agbụ ọlụ Ebune ya
proverbs.english: Where they stand to curse Ebune, they stand to undo it for Ebune; 'Iyi bụ ebune' means 'Iyi kill, do not kill.'

proverbs.igbo: Ya k'ẹ gbu k'ọ jị melue ọlị ọma nọ
proverbs.english: That is why they do it so well to Esa who wanted to buy okpụ prepared for mmụọ.

proverbs.igbo: Anyị amaghị ije, anyị enweghị afọ ụkwụ.
proverbs.english: We cannot go a journey, we have not a calf (of the leg).
proverbs.usage: If a traveller brings nothing new to buy why does he travel.

proverbs.igbo: Ha amaghị ọ bụ ome ruo abụọ
proverbs.english: They don't know virgin witch.
proverbs.usage: When a man cannot find a thief.

proverbs.igbo: Ụzọ adịghị afịa nkịta.
proverbs.english: A dog does not miss the way.

proverbs.igbo: Onye na-adọ onye aka eze na-ewetara onwe ya ihere.
proverbs.english: He that reproves a scorner inflicts shame on himself.

proverbs.igbo: Onye na-asa enweghị iro.
proverbs.english: A good humoured man has no enemy.

proverbs.igbo: Onye na-akpọ onye na-akpagbu ya iyi; afọ ya ka ọ na-akpọ, afọ ya bụ isi na-akpagbu ya.
proverbs.english: If a man curses with iyi one who troubles him, it is his belly he curses; it is his belly that first troubles him.
proverbs.usage: If a man curses his brother he curses himself.

proverbs.igbo: Anya dinta hụrụ agụ, obi m adịghị eje.
proverbs.english: The hunter sees a leopard but does not shoot.

proverbs.igbo: Ụgwọ afọ adịghị akwụ ụgwọ.
proverbs.english: Debt of the stomach has no redemption; one has to sell treasures rather than die.

proverbs.igbo: Nzuzo adịghị ezo n'ọbụm.
proverbs.english: There is no hiding place in the open space (sand bank).

proverbs.igbo: Osisi pụta ihu adịghị emikpu ụgbọ.
proverbs.english: A stick on the surface cannot sink the boat; a trap that is seen is useless.

proverbs.igbo: Nye m nri ka afọ ju m, unu ajụzina m ebe m na-alaru.
proverbs.english: Give me food to fill my belly; don't ask where I sleep.
proverbs.usage: Let me deal with the matter.

proverbs.igbo: Ọ dịghị onye ma ebe ụwa si abịa, ma ihe jidere igwe.
proverbs.english: No one knows whence earth comes nor what holds sky.
proverbs.usage: When relatives in ebo treat a man ill.

proverbs.igbo: Ha adịghị ebu otu akpa ruo Idu.
proverbs.english: They don't pick up a load and reach Idu at one go; a word does not finish.

proverbs.igbo: Ọnwụ dịkebụ ụtụ, ọ na-eri ihe nwere ajị.
proverbs.english: If the penis is not dead, it can eat what has a beard.
proverbs.usage: One who is absent gets no share.

proverbs.igbo: Oyibo dị ngala
proverbs.english: All white men are proud.

proverbs.igbo: Nkụ adịghị ebu igu abụ ọsọ
proverbs.english: The wood does not take the palm leaf and run away.
proverbs.usage: By a man to whom a visit is announced.

proverbs.igbo: Ọkụ nsi adịghị akọ ala
proverbs.english: A poisoner cannot poison the ground.

proverbs.igbo: Onye chọrọ, achọta
proverbs.english: Who seeks, finds.

proverbs.igbo: Ana m achọ ihe adịghị ahụ
proverbs.english: I want something that is not seen.

proverbs.igbo: Ụta m na-agba, ọkpụkpọ nye m aka
proverbs.english: Bow I shoot, ring net I handle.
proverbs.usage: When a young man asks another what he can do.

proverbs.igbo: Anụ soro enwe, ọ gbajie aka
proverbs.english: Beast follows monkey, it breaks its hand (leg).
proverbs.usage: Of man who tries to imitate another.

proverbs.igbo: Okpọnụ bụ ohu n'ebo ya
proverbs.english: A single man is a slave in his ebo.

proverbs.igbo: Obodo abụọ mụ nkita; obodo na-ebo nni mụrụ ya n'aka ekpe; obodo na-ata ụtọ mụrụ ya n'aka nri; ya mere nkita enweghị ikè.
proverbs.english: Two towns bore dog; the town that seizes food bore it in the left hand (antelope), the town that eats sweet things bore it in the right hand (cat); that makes dog have no rump.
proverbs.usage: Animals were choosing a king; dog was selected but ran to eat food offered to it and was rejected; dog's father comes from antelope, dog's mother from cat, hence antelope runs like a dog, cat eats sweet things.

proverbs.igbo: Tọnọ mụ, tọnọ mụ, ọ mụ gịnị?
proverbs.english: Provide for children even if the father starves (mother says).
